## 2026-09-29 — FINAL CLOSURE: Eurosender Sandbox investigation (Support-confirmed)

**Trigger:** official Eurosender Support response, cited verbatim by the owner. This closes the open items from Phase 26 without further Sandbox probing of `order_tracking_ready` / `delivery_status_updated` / full customs progression.

### Confirmed by Eurosender Support
- `order_label_ready`, `order_submitted_to_courier`, `order_cancelled`: valid and testable in Sandbox — matches this project's own live evidence (17 genuine Sandbox deliveries, Phase 26).
- `order_tracking_ready` and `delivery_status_updated`: **effectively Production-only** — Sandbox does not simulate real courier tracking. **Classification finalized: PRODUCTION-ONLY / SANDBOX LIMITATION CONFIRMED BY EUROSENDER.** No further attempts will be made to trigger these in Sandbox.
- Sandbox does not execute the full customs-review/courier-submission lifecycle end to end — matches this project's observation that order `718586-26` never advanced past `Awaiting customs documentation`.
- A non-2xx from the pickup endpoint should be treated as "no availability," falling back to Eurosender's automatic/default pickup.
- The reproducible HTTP 500 on `/v1/pickup/{orderCode}` (found in Phase 26, order `523527-26`, ×4 reproductions) has been forwarded by Eurosender to their technical team — **BLOCKED on Eurosender's side, not an application defect.**
- Sandbox quote instability (the transient `400 "Syntax error"` burst observed in Phase 26) is known Sandbox behavior, not an application defect, when the request is correctly formatted.
- Sandbox prices are not live/real prices; Production/API prices must be used for real customer-facing pricing (no change needed here — the app already never uses Eurosender's Sandbox price as a customer-facing number; `_customer_price_fields` is the only price source shown to customers, per the platform's standing pricing rule).
- VAT/B2B activation requires Eurosender's requested company/VAT documentation — an owner/business task, not a code task.

### Capability classifications — FINALIZED
**PASS:** `order_label_ready`, `order_submitted_to_courier`, `order_cancelled`, order creation, label/document retrieval, tracking read API, proforma submission.
**PRODUCTION-ONLY / SANDBOX LIMITATION CONFIRMED BY EUROSENDER:** `order_tracking_ready`, `delivery_status_updated`, full customs-route progression beyond what Sandbox simulates.

### Application defect — verified fixed (Phase 26 fix, re-confirmed here)
**Root cause:** tracking was persisted only in the `order_tracking_ready` handler. Since that event is Production-only, the Sandbox/Production-common case — a real tracking number already present in the `order_submitted_to_courier` payload — left `orders.tracking_number = NULL` forever.
**Fix:** single shared `_apply_tracking_codes()` in `routes/eurosender_webhook.py`, called from BOTH `order_submitted_to_courier` and `order_tracking_ready` — one tracking-persistence path, not two. Idempotent (`order.tracking_number == tracking_number` short-circuits before any DB write or notification, so re-delivery or double-firing never double-notifies the customer). Preserves the last-leg-for-multi-carrier rule and the never-regress-terminal-status rule.
**Verified (unchanged from Phase 26, re-run today):** `order_submitted_to_courier` with tracking → number + URL persisted, supplier payment → `tracking_received`, exactly one customer notification (live real Sandbox order `ASF-P26-E2E-3`, deleted afterward). `order_tracking_ready` continues to work standalone (its own dedicated tests still pass) for whenever Production actually emits it. Duplicate delivery of the same tracking number → 0 additional notifications (unit-tested: `test_same_tracking_number_arriving_twice_never_double_notifies`).
**Regression:** `test_eurosender_webhook.py` 41/41, `test_eurosender_fulfillment.py` + `test_eurosender_order_service.py` 28/28, full Eurosender suite 207/207, named direct regressions 64/64 — all re-run fresh today, identical to Phase 26's counts (no new tests added this closure, none needed).

### Pickup HTTP 500 handling — verified, NO code change made
Traced every caller of pickup scheduling: `independentPickup` is set nowhere in the codebase (`grep independentPickup` across all production `.py` files returns zero results) and `create_shipment()`'s payload never includes it, so it always defaults to `false` per Eurosender's own schema. **The application never calls `/v1/pickup/{orderCode}` or its availability endpoint in the real order-creation flow at all** — every order this app creates uses Eurosender's automatic/default pickup already, by construction, never independent pickup. Eurosender Support's guidance ("non-2xx -> no availability -> automatic fallback") describes behavior for a code path this application does not use. **The application already satisfies the required outcome — trivially, by never opting into independent pickup — and no code change is needed or was made.** The reproducible 500 discovered in Phase 26 was from a direct diagnostic call (`_do_request` against `/v1/pickup/523527-26`, order created specifically for that test, no application code involved) and cannot occur via any real order the app creates today.

### FOLLOW-UP / DESIGN DECISION REQUIRED (unchanged, not touched this closure)
Webhook dedup key is set BEFORE `handle_event()` runs, and handler exceptions return HTTP 200 (swallowed). A transient DB error during handling would lose that webhook permanently — Eurosender won't retry a 200, and the dedup key would block any coincidental future retry regardless. Recommended fix (NOT implemented, needs explicit owner approval since it changes retry semantics): move the dedup-key `SET` to after a successful `db.commit()`, and return a 5xx (not 200) on a genuine handler exception so Eurosender's own retry mechanism (confirmed to exist — Phase 20 evidence, ids 10790/10793 retried after 401s) can recover it.

### Safety
Production API calls: 0. Sandbox mutations: 0 (read-only verification only). `EUROSENDER_ENABLED=False`, `EUROSENDER_SANDBOX=True`, allowlist empty. Test rows: 0 remain (orders/user re-confirmed deleted). UK test supplier still `is_active=false`. Car-Parts.ie untouched (`shipping_info` still NULL). Temporary webhook capture code: 0 markers remain, 0 capture files remain (both re-confirmed).

**Status: CLOSED.** Not committed, not pushed — awaiting explicit approval.

## 2026-09-29 — FINAL PHASE: Eurosender production integration — root-cause closure

**Scope:** full lifecycle audit + close every real fixable defect, per the Eurosender Support-confirmed facts already recorded (2026-09-29 closure entry above) and the committed tracking fix (`90903b1`).

### Full lifecycle audit (traced end to end, real code read, not assumed)
`trigger_supplier_fulfillment` (routes/utils.py) → `handle_eligible_suppliers` → `_attempt_shipment` → pickup extraction (`_extract_pickup_from_shipping_info`) → item categories → `evaluate_and_create_shipment` (dimension/weight/HS/declared-value gates, all fail-closed to `MANUAL_REVIEW`, never guess) → `create_shipment` → `_submit_proforma` when `awaiting_customs` → `_persist_result` (order + supplier_payment) → webhook route → `handle_event` (5 branches) → `_apply_tracking_codes` (shared) → `_persist_result`-equivalent writes → notification. Every state transition, DB write, and external call in this chain was re-read this session; no additional business-logic defect was found beyond the two below.

### DEFECT 1 (root-caused and FIXED): webhook retry/dedup could permanently lose a webhook
**Root cause:** the Redis dedup key was written BEFORE `handle_event()` ran, and a handler exception was swallowed behind an HTTP 200. A transient DB/application failure mid-processing therefore left the webhook (a) not actually applied AND (b) marked "seen" — Eurosender never retries a 200, so that event was gone forever, with no recoverable trace.
**Fix (`routes/eurosender_webhook.py`):** the dedup key is now a read-only fast-path check before processing, and is only ever WRITTEN after `handle_event()` + `db.commit()` both succeed. A handler exception now rolls back and returns **503** (not 200) — a genuine invitation for Eurosender's own confirmed retry mechanism (Phase 20: ids 10790/10793 retried after 401s) to redeliver it. No dedup key is ever set for a failed attempt, so the retry is not suppressed.
**Business-logic idempotency (defense in depth, since Redis is explicitly best-effort — `_get_redis_safe()` already falls back to "continue without dedup" if Redis is down):** `order_cancelled` was the one handler with an unconditional side effect (an admin `Notification` on every call) — now guarded with `if order.eurosender_status == "cancelled": return` before doing anything, so a duplicate delivery can never double-alert regardless of Redis's state. The other four handlers were already naturally idempotent (status writes are no-ops on an unchanged value or guarded by `not in _TERMINAL_OR_ADVANCED`; `_apply_tracking_codes` already short-circuits on an unchanged tracking number) — verified by tracing each branch, not assumed.
**Also removed:** a redundant inner `await db.commit()` inside `order_cancelled` — the route's single commit (after `handle_event` returns) is now the one transaction boundary, consistent with "processing failure ⇒ nothing claims success."
**Regression (6 new tests, Tests A-E from the spec + F already covered by Phase 26's tracking tests):** normal delivery applies once and marks dedup; a simulated processing failure returns ≥500 and does NOT mark dedup; the same webhook redelivered after a failure applies exactly once and then marks dedup; a duplicate after success never reaches `handle_event` again; an invalid signature never poisons dedup for a later valid delivery of the same id; `order_cancelled` redelivered against an already-cancelled order sends zero additional alerts.
**Real Sandbox retry injection (task section 5):** attempted a controlled test where the live route deliberately returns a temporary 5xx once for a genuine delivery, then restores normal handling. **This exact action was denied by the Claude Code auto-mode permission classifier** (same as the identical attempt in Phase 26) — not bypassed. Falling back exactly as the task's own instruction anticipates: the application-level semantics are fully verified by the 6 deterministic tests above using the real, unmocked route and verifier, with only `handle_event` mocked to simulate the failure; the external fact that Eurosender itself retries a non-2xx delivery is independently already proven (Phase 20 live evidence).

### DEFECT 2 (root-caused and FIXED): production was structurally unreachable, and `EUROSENDER_ENABLED` had no real effect
**Root cause — outbound (`eurosender_adapter.py`):** `_preflight()` raised `EurosenderProductionBlocked` on ANY resolved production URL, unconditionally — regardless of `EUROSENDER_ENABLED`. This was a correct, deliberate scope limiter for the sandbox-development phase, but it directly contradicts this project's own documented architecture ("EUROSENDER_ENABLED is the actual production kill switch" — explicitly named as a requirement to verify in this closure) and made every earlier piece of "production readiness" work (credential wiring, config hardening) unverifiable and pointless, since production could never be reached no matter what was configured.
**Root cause — inbound (`routes/eurosender_webhook.py`):** the webhook route independently refused with `501` whenever `EUROSENDER_SANDBOX` was falsy, unconditionally. Undiscovered until now, this is the more dangerous of the two: the moment the owner ever sets `EUROSENDER_SANDBOX=0` to activate production, this endpoint would start **permanently rejecting every real Eurosender webhook** (label_ready/submitted_to_courier/tracking_ready/cancelled/delivery_status_updated) with 501 — silently breaking order-status tracking for every real production customer order, with no error visible anywhere except a 501 in nginx's access log.
**Fix:** both gates now key off `EUROSENDER_ENABLED` (the adapter) / `EUROSENDER_ENABLED OR EUROSENDER_SANDBOX` (the webhook route — refuses only when disabled in both directions), matching the kill-switch architecture already documented and used everywhere else in this integration (`eurosender_routing.is_eurosender_eligible`). **Today's real config is functionally UNCHANGED** — `EUROSENDER_ENABLED=False` (unset) and `EUROSENDER_SANDBOX` unset (defaults True) in `.env`, verified live before and after — production remains exactly as unreachable as before. The only behavioral change is that production becomes reachable once the owner explicitly flips both real config values AND supplies real production credentials — never done in this session.
**Regression:** 3 new adapter tests confirm production stays blocked today (no kill switch), stays blocked with the kill switch alone but no key, and DOES proceed only with both the kill switch AND a real key present (verified with a fake HTTP client — no real network call). 3 new webhook-route tests mirror this for the inbound side, including the exact historic-bug scenario (`SANDBOX=0 + ENABLED=1` must NOT 501).

### DEFECT 3 (root-caused and FIXED): Sandbox and Production credentials shared one env var each
**Root cause:** `api_key()` and `webhook_secret()` each read a single, non-environment-specific env var (`EUROSENDER_API_KEY`, `EUROSENDER_WEBHOOK_SECRET`). Combined with Defect 2, this meant: the moment someone flipped `EUROSENDER_SANDBOX=0`, the code would use whatever was in the SAME variable that has only ever held the Sandbox credential throughout this entire project — i.e., the Sandbox API key and webhook signing secret would silently be sent to the real Production endpoint.
**Fix:** `api_key()`/`webhook_secret()` now select `EUROSENDER_SANDBOX_*` or `EUROSENDER_PRODUCTION_*` based on `sandbox_mode()`. Sandbox mode ONLY falls back to the legacy single var (since that's genuinely what it has always held) — backward-compatible, zero `.env` changes required, verified live (`api_key_set=True`, `webhook_secret_set=True`, unchanged after this fix). Production mode has NO fallback to the legacy var — it requires the dedicated `EUROSENDER_PRODUCTION_API_KEY`/`EUROSENDER_PRODUCTION_WEBHOOK_SECRET` to be set explicitly, or `EurosenderNotConfigured` is raised before any network call (fails safe, per section 7's requirement).
**Wiring:** `docker-compose.yml` updated to pass through the 4 new env vars (empty-default, same safe pattern as the existing ones) — without this, setting the new vars in `.env` alone would never have reached the container. Applied via `docker compose up -d backend` (compose file changed, per this repo's own deployment rule) — container recreated, health 200, real config re-verified unchanged.
**Regression:** 4 new config tests (legacy-name backward compatibility, dedicated-var precedence, and the legacy var proven NOT to leak into production).

### Non-findings (verified, no change needed)
- **Pickup handling (section 15):** re-confirmed `independentPickup` is set nowhere in production code (`grep` across the whole backend, zero hits outside tests) — the app still never calls `/v1/pickup/{orderCode}`, so Eurosender's non-2xx-fallback guidance describes a path this app doesn't use. No code needed.
- **HS gate (B4, section 17):** re-read `classify_hs`/`_build_packages_and_gates` — unchanged, still fails closed to `MANUAL_REVIEW`, no universal fallback code. No loosening made or needed.
- **B5 supplier data:** UK test supplier still `is_active=false`; Car-Parts.ie still untouched (`shipping_info` NULL); no guessed address inserted.
- **Security audit (section 19):** HMAC over exact raw bytes + `hmac.compare_digest` (unchanged, Phase 19/22-verified); signature checked before any parse/dedup/handling (unchanged); `_scrub()` + `_raise_for_status_safe()` are the sole HTTP-error path for every adapter method (2 call sites, both covered) — no secret can leak through an exception message; grepped for any `logger.*` call that might dump a payload/body/response — none found beyond safe order codes/statuses; grepped for `TEMP-CAPTURE`/`TEMP-FAILONCE`/`TEMP-DIAG`/test-supplier-UUID/test-order-codes in production code — zero hits (only 2 historical evidence references inside docstring comments, not executable code).
- **Pricing (section 18):** unchanged — `_customer_price_fields` remains the only customer-facing price source platform-wide; this Eurosender work never touches customer pricing; Sandbox prices were never used as production prices anywhere in this codebase.

### Test results (full re-run, this session)
Eurosender suite: **222/222** (was 207 after the committed tracking fix; +15 this closure: 6 retry/dedup + 3 route-availability-gate + 6 adapter production-gate/credential-separation). Named direct regressions: **64/64** (unchanged). `test_fitment_step0_release_gate.py`/`test_db_network_hardening.py`: 4/7 — the same 3 pre-existing, unrelated failures (routes/parts.py caching logic; docker-compose.yml not bind-mounted inside the test container) confirmed again this session, untouched by this work.

### Real API operations this session
Sandbox API calls: 0 (only `grep`/code reads/unit tests — no live Eurosender call was made this closure). Production API calls: **0**. Production mutations: **0**. Production orders: **0**.

### External dependency (genuine, not invented)
**EXTERNAL DEPENDENCY — WAITING FOR EUROSENDER PRODUCTION CREDENTIALS.** No real `EUROSENDER_PRODUCTION_API_KEY` / `EUROSENDER_PRODUCTION_WEBHOOK_SECRET` exist yet (Eurosender has been asked to provide them). The code is now correctly wired to receive and use them the moment they exist, gated by the same `EUROSENDER_ENABLED` kill switch and requiring the owner to explicitly set `EUROSENDER_SANDBOX=0` — neither was touched this session. No credential was invented, guessed, or hard-coded.

**Status: TECHNICALLY CLOSED**, subject only to the external credential dependency above. Not committed, not pushed — awaiting explicit approval.

**Scheduler-triggered, not manually invoked.** Job `sync_prices:2026-09-30T03:15:30.678990`, started 03:15:30Z, completed 04:29:47Z (~74 min). Confirmed via the scheduler's own `[PriceSync] done — updated=109 avail_changes=0 errors=0` log line and its own `AliExpress price sync: checking 249 parts (targeting=discovery)` / `AliExpress price sync complete: {...}` lines — no admin endpoint, no direct `sync_prices()`/`sync_aliexpress_prices()` call, no manual trigger of any kind was used to produce this cycle; it fired at its own naturally-computed due time (the loop's own math from the prior 2026-09-29 03:15:27Z completion + 24h interval).

**Report:** `parts_checked=249` (limit 2000; finite candidate pool — not a failure) · `parts_updated=109` · `parts_not_found=133` · `sku_conflicts=7` · `discovery_queries=150` · `candidates_added=358` · `api_calls=515` (cross-checked: 515−150 discovery−249 search = 116 product.get calls = 109 updated + 7 conflicts, exact — the same identity verified on 8 prior cycles) · `api_call_limit_hits=0` · `searches_unconfirmed=0`, `search_failure_kinds={}`, `search_aborted=False` · `errors=[]`.

**Stage 3 fix (transient-search-failure protection):** **not naturally exercised this cycle** (`searches_unconfirmed=0`) — no regression evidence either way; the mechanism simply had nothing to catch this run. Not a defect.

**Data integrity (independently verified, not from the self-report):** candidates cited 1207→1316, no_match 1837→1977, matched 1888→1997 (Δmatched=109, exact match to `parts_updated`); AliExpress offers 1890→1999 (Δ=109, exact); AliExpress price_history 1899→2008 (Δ=109, exact, all `source='aliexpress_sync'`); 0 duplicate offers (by SKU and by part); 0 OEM/base-price pollution; 0 non-AliExpress `supplier_parts` rows touched in the run window; `parts_catalog` row count unchanged (4,607,422). Job registry: exactly one `sync_prices` row in the run window, no overlap; Redis lock free both before and after.

**Pricing safety — independently verified via the canonical function itself, not reimplemented:** 3 sampled new offers' raw costs (182.54 / 35.43 / 55.23 ₪) run through `routes.parts._customer_price_fields` produced 264.68 / 51.37 / 80.08 ₪ (cost×1.45, 0% VAT — AliExpress is foreign/CN), confirming no bypass and no raw-cost exposure. All new offers classified `aftermarket` (never `oem`).

**CONFOUNDER 1 — unrelated OOM, unattributable to Stage 3.** A genuine kernel OOM killed `uvicorn` (and, in the same event, a `chrome-headless` process in the same container) at 2026-09-29 23:49:32 UTC — confirmed via `dmesg`, matched to the exact running `autospare_backend` container ID. The container's current `StartedAt` (2026-09-30T02:49:08Z) is ~3 hours after that kill, an unusually long gap for a simple `unless-stopped` auto-restart; the cause of that specific delay is **not established** (not investigated further — out of scope) and no restart was performed by this session. Because the restart happened well before the natural due time, the loop's one-time wait recomputation still landed on the same natural due time (~03:15Z) — the resulting cycle is not itself a product of the restart's timing, only enabled by it (the loop had to re-arm after the crash).

**CONFOUNDER 2 — the still-unapproved `get_part_details()` schema fix is live and materially changed this run's shape.** That fix (staged 2026-09-29, never approved, never deployed by this session — it became live purely as a side effect of an earlier unrelated OOM restart) was exercised extensively this cycle: `parts_images_added=453` for only 109 updated parts (≈4.2 images/part) — independently confirmed by sampling: **85 of 109 new offers got exactly 5 images** (the per-part cap), several got more (pre-existing images from other suppliers summed in), and only **7 of 109** still show the old single-image shape. This is a direct, measurable consequence of `get_part_details()` now succeeding instead of always returning `None` — **this improvement belongs to that separate, not-yet-approved fix, not to Stage 3**, and is recorded here only to correctly attribute it, not to claim it as a Stage 3 result.

**Unproven:** the AliExpress external call quota remains unproven beyond this run's own observed 515 calls / 0 `ApiCallLimit` events. The 3-hour OOM-to-restart gap's cause is unproven.

**Final status: PASS — Stage 3 verified through the real scheduler path.** No commit, no push.

## 2026-10-02 — Issue #51: Facebook group scanner OOM — batched scan fix: VERIFIED

**Root cause:** `_group_scan_loop()` in `BACKEND_API_ROUTES.py` called `facebook_group_scan()` → `agent.scan_groups(all_386_groups)` in a single call. `scan_groups()` opens ONE `FacebookSession` (= one Chrome process via Playwright persistent context) for the entire group list. One Chrome session iterating 386 groups accumulates V8 heap + page state over ~2.7 hours, growing from ~200 MB RSS at session start to ~850 MB at end, filling the 4 GB backend container limit and triggering an OOM kill.

**Why the existing `run_group_scanner()` (BATCH=10) was NOT wired in:** it is missing `has_active_draft()`, `draft_budget_per_cycle()`, `record_scan_run()`, `maybe_autonomous_group_post()`, and `notify_owner()` with cooldown — the full NOA approval-gated pipeline that `_group_scan_loop()` owns downstream.

**Fix (BACKEND_API_ROUTES.py lines 2919–3001):** replaced the single `facebook_group_scan()` call inside `_group_scan_loop()` with an inline batched loop:
- Queries `group_targets` (platform=facebook, status≠rejected) ordered by `last_posted_at NULLS FIRST, created_at` — same ordering as `group_scanner._load_all_discovered_groups()`
- Slices into batches of `SOCIAL_GROUP_SCAN_BATCH_SIZE` (default `10`, env-overridable)
- Each batch: `await GroupAgent().scan_groups(batch)` — ONE Chrome lifecycle per batch (each `scan_groups()` call is wrapped in `async with FacebookSession()`, which launches and closes Chrome via `_start()`/`_stop()`)
- Chrome RSS at batch end: `context.close()` flushes the profile then Playwright stops Chrome → next batch starts clean
- Discoveries + telemetry accumulated across batches into `_all_disc` / `_agg_tel`
- `session_failed=True` on any batch → halts remaining batches immediately (authentication lost, no point continuing)
- Any batch exception caught → logged as warning + added to `_batch_errors`; other batches continue
- Produces a `types.SimpleNamespace(status, data, error)` matching the shape that all existing downstream code (`draft_budget_per_cycle`, `has_active_draft`, LLM draft loop, `record_scan_run`, `notify_owner`) already consumes — zero downstream changes

**What is unchanged:**
- `social/tools.py::facebook_group_scan()` — manual/owner-console path, still calls `scan_groups(all)` in one shot
- All NOA drafting/approval/record scaffolding in `_group_scan_loop()` after the scan
- Drafting threshold: `suggested_action in ("comment","post")` — NOT score >= 0.25
- `NOA_GROUP_DRAFT_MAX_PER_CYCLE` budget cap
- `has_active_draft()` pre-LLM-call check
- `record_scan_run()` call with full aggregated totals
- Autonomous post gate, notify_owner cooldown

**Memory reduction (expected):** each 10-group batch takes ~2–4 min vs ~2.7 h for 386. Peak Chrome RSS stays in the 200–300 MB range per batch rather than accumulating to ~850 MB. 39 × (small peak) replaces 1 × (large accumulated peak).

**Regression tests added:** `backend/tests/test_group_scan_batching.py` — 20 tests, **20/20 PASSED** (1.11s):
1. 386 groups → 38×10 + 1×6 = 39 batches (arithmetic verified)
2. `scan_groups()` called once per batch, not once for all groups
3. Discoveries aggregated from all batches
4. Telemetry fields summed across batches
5. Production filter uses `suggested_action in ("comment","post")`, not `score >= 0.25`
6. "monitor" discovery (0.2 ≤ score < 0.4) is NOT drafted
7. score=0.25 / action="monitor" → not drafted
8. score=0.40 / action="comment" → drafted
9. `draft_budget_caps_llm_calls` — budget honored
10. `NOA_GROUP_DRAFT_MAX_PER_CYCLE` env var respected
11. `has_active_draft()` skip prevents LLM call
12. `record_scan_run()` receives complete aggregated cycle totals
13. Failed batch does not repeat already-completed batches
14. `session_failed` halts remaining batches and is propagated
15-20. `SimpleNamespace` result contract for success, session_failed, and batch_error cases

**Files changed:**
- `backend/BACKEND_API_ROUTES.py` — lines 2919–3001: batched group scan replacing single `facebook_group_scan()` call
- `backend/tests/test_group_scan_batching.py` — new (20 regression tests)

**Safety constraints honored (zero production impact):**
- NO production scan execution
- NO scheduler trigger
- NO container restart / recreation / stop
- NO docker resource-limit changes
- NO swap changes
- NO AliExpress interruption
- NO modification to `facebook_group_scan()` (manual path)
- NO change to NOA approval semantics / drafting threshold / budget / `has_active_draft` / `record_scan_run`

**Status: VERIFIED** — fix live on disk (bind-mount active), tests 20/20 in container; will take effect on the next natural scheduler fire (~daily) without any restart.

**Remaining limitation:** the fix reduces Chrome RSS per-batch but does not eliminate accumulation within a single batch (10 groups still share one Chrome session). If a single group's page hangs for a long time, that batch's Chrome still accumulates. `SOCIAL_GROUP_SCAN_BATCH_SIZE=5` or lower can be set without a restart if needed.

## 2026-10-04 — Email Agent foundation: Gmail read, classification, context, policy, draft-only

**Goal:** a production-grade foundation for an Email Agent on the business mailbox. This phase must not send email.

**Finding (inventory, verified in code and live):**
- The backend had an outbound-only email path (`routes/email_utils.py`, Gmail SMTP app password). Nothing read the mailbox.
- The only Google OAuth grant in `.env` is the YouTube one. Live check: token refresh succeeds, granted scope is `youtube.force-ssl` only, `GET gmail/v1/users/me/profile` returns 403 `insufficient authentication scopes`. No `GMAIL_*` variable exists.
- The closest existing architecture is NOA's inbound engine (`social/engagement.py`: record once, draft, human decides), so the Email Agent follows that shape instead of adding a second agent framework.

**Built:** package `backend/email_agent/` (config, redaction, gmail_client, normalize, senders, context, classifier, policy, drafts, store, agent, loop); `routes/email_agent_routes.py` (`GET /api/v1/system/email-agent`, `X-Collect-Secret`); `maintenance/email_agent_cli.py`; `maintenance/gmail_oauth_setup.py` (host-side consent URL + code exchange into `.env`, prints no secret); migration `alembic_pii/versions/0039_email_agent_messages.py`; loop + router registered in `BACKEND_API_ROUTES.py`; env pass-throughs in `docker-compose.yml`; `docs/EMAIL_AGENT.md`.

**No-send boundary (six layers):** no send method on the client; a six-endpoint allowlist (`GET profile|messages|messages/{id}|threads/{id}|drafts/{id}`, `POST drafts`) checked before every request; `policy.send_allowed()` returns False unconditionally; every decision `sendable=False`; `CHECK (sendable = false)` on the table; `POST drafts` never auto-retried.

**Bugs caught before shipping (by the tests, not in production):**
- `received_at` was bound as an ISO string into `CAST(:x AS timestamptz)`; asyncpg requires a datetime. Caught by the store test against real Postgres, fixed in `store.save_result`.
- A Gmail part whose `body` is not an object crashed normalization; invalid base64 was decoded to garbage instead of rejected. Both fixed in `normalize.py`.

**Existing issue revealed and fixed:** `tests/test_whatsapp_empty_body_guard.py` failed (8 tests, `RuntimeError: There is no current event loop`) whenever an async test file ran before it, e.g. `tests/test_whatsapp_test_isolation.py`. Root cause: its `_run()` helper used `asyncio.get_event_loop().run_until_complete()`, which fails once pytest-asyncio has closed the loop. Reproduced with only those two pre-existing files. Fix: `asyncio.run(coro)`. Now 8/8 pass in any order.

**Verification:**
- VERIFIED — `tests/test_email_agent.py`: 104 passed (103 + the opt-in real-Postgres store test on a session TEMP table; the test asserts the table is temporary and that nothing remains afterwards).
- VERIFIED — migration 0039 DDL executed inside a transaction on the PII DB and rolled back (table + 3 indexes created, `to_regclass` NULL after rollback); `alembic heads` shows the single head `0039_email_agent_messages`.
- VERIFIED — context SQL against live data, SELECT only: a real order + its account resolves and passes the primary-key re-check; the same order cited by a different sender is `sender_mismatch` with no references; a real supplier website domain resolves.
- VERIFIED — live OAuth through `GmailClient` with the existing YouTube-scoped grant: token refresh OK, Gmail denies the scope, the agent reports `error_kind=scope`, processes 0 messages. HTTP calls made: `POST oauth2 token`, `GET gmail profile`.

## #68 — Stitch homepage: `edit_screens` reports success without persisting; all four "Marketplace Home" screens were abridged — 2026-10-05

**How it was found.** A prior session recorded Stitch screen `d45b6e30ebc947588126c1f068dc2223` ("AutoSpareFinder - Marketplace Home", 2560x3396) as the successful desktop homepage. That conclusion came from a **title match in `list_screens` plus the presence of an `htmlCode` entry** — the content was never fetched. Downloading it this session showed its html `<title>` is *"AutoSpare - High Performance Parts"*, its footer reads *"© 2024 AUTOSPARE PERFORMANCE. ENGINEERED FOR SPEED."*, and its 63 text nodes contain no categories, no vehicles, no why-us, no comparison table and no AI section. Exactly the failure mode in CLAUDE.md §1: *never pick a resource as "the" target of a task by name-match alone.*

**Finding 1 — every Stitch homepage screen is abridged.** All four desktop screens carrying marketplace-home titles were downloaded and their visible text parsed. Each is the same shape: header + hero + four "Featured Parts" cards + footer. **Three of the eight required sections**; the hero search is a single input, not the dual-mode vehicle/part panel. Missing from all four: Popular Categories, Popular Vehicles, Why AutoSpareFinder, Supplier/Price Comparison, AI Chat CTA. Stitch collapses a long multi-section brief to its own template rather than honouring it.

**Finding 2 (the real bug) — `edit_screens` does not commit.** Three separate edits against `3db3e13b610049b8bf41babb9f3d3196` each returned a detailed success payload naming the exact DOM operations, selectors and `verified_html_context`. Afterwards the stored HTML was **byte-identical (17,240 bytes)**, the `htmlCode` file id was unchanged (`0abceaf642734f79b11eaec20b7a263b`), the screenshot file id was unchanged, `list_screens` still returned 19 screens, and the rendered screenshot still showed "Find Your Perfect Part", a single search input and "© 2024". **Treat the `edit_screens` response as a plan, not a commit** — always re-download the HTML and compare bytes.

**Finding 3 — prompt size governs the timeout.** `generate_screen_from_text` (MOBILE) timed out twice with no screen created, and a six-section `edit_screens` prompt timed out. A two-change prompt against the same screen returned in seconds. Reads (`list_screens`, `get_screen`) were never affected.

**Delivered instead:** `.stitch/designs/homepage.html` — the full eight-section homepage built directly to `.stitch/DESIGN.md` tokens (Void Black `#0F1218`, Electric Blue `#0EA5E9`, 6px geometric buttons, speed-line dividers, AI glow `0 0 24px rgba(14,165,233,.40)`, Inter + JetBrains Mono), no light backgrounds and no pill buttons. Supplier names in the comparison table are masked per the `_mask_supplier` rule.

**Verification (Playwright, headless Chromium, full-page):**
- VERIFIED — all 8 sections render: sticky header, hero + dual-mode search + trust bar, 10 categories, 4 vehicles, 4 why-cards, 3-row comparison table with verified-fit badge, AI CTA with Hebrew chat bubbles and glow, 4-column footer reading "© 2026 AutoSpareFinder".
- VERIFIED — zero horizontal overflow at 1440, 1280, 834, 768, 390 and 360 px.
- VERIFIED — RTL (`dir="rtl"`) mirrors correctly: nav order reverses, logo moves right, hero art swaps side, Make/Model/Year reverse to Year/Model/Make, prices and OEM codes stay LTR via `unicode-bidi:isolate`.

Fixed by collapsing the nav to a burger at ≤900px and shrinking the header controls at ≤640px. Re-verified clean at all six widths.

## 2026-10-06 — Gmail OAuth: "no code after consent" root-caused; setup helper now captures the redirect itself

**Report:** the owner approved the Gmail consent screen (twice, 2026-10-04) and saw no `?code=` in the browser.

**Root cause (VERIFIED from the nginx access log):** Google did return the code both times. Two requests reached the edge nginx: `GET /?iss=https://accounts.google.com&code=…&scope=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly` at 20:17:34 and 20:20:58 UTC, HTTP 200, Referer `https://accounts.google.com/`. No `error` parameter. Requests made by the same page afterwards (assets, `/api/v1/parts/categories` 20 s later, the click to `/login` two minutes later) still carried the full URL with the code in their `Referer`, so nothing on our side removed it: nginx `location /` serves `index.html` with no redirect, and the frontend has no code that rewrites the query on `/`. The redirect URI is simply the public homepage, which renders normally. The flow depended on a person spotting the code in a long address-bar URL and copying it.

**Google-side configuration (VERIFIED by behaviour, console not accessed):** Google only redirects to a URI registered on the client, and it redirected to exactly `https://autosparefinder.co.il/` with a code, so the redirect URI and the `gmail.readonly` scope are accepted for client `614571826604-cmdavo…`. Whether the Gmail API is enabled in the project is still unverified (it only shows on the first Gmail call).

**Fix:** `backend/maintenance/gmail_oauth_setup.py` — `auth-url` adds a one-time `state` (kept in a 0600 file outside the repo, valid 1 h); new `callback-status` finds the redirect with that `state` in the nginx access log and reports only non-secret facts; `exchange` without `--code` takes the code from that redirect, refusing a missing, errored or older-than-8-minutes callback. No code, token or secret is printed. Tests: `backend/tests/test_gmail_oauth_setup.py` (9).

**Verification:** tests 112 passed, 1 skipped (`test_gmail_oauth_setup.py` + `test_email_agent.py`). Live trace with a fake code: issued a URL, sent `GET https://autosparefinder.co.il/?state=<ours>&iss=…&code=<fake>&scope=…gmail.readonly` (200, no redirect), `callback-status` then reported `callback_received: true, code_present: true, code_fresh: true, granted_scope: gmail.readonly`. No token exchange performed; `.env` has no `GMAIL_OAUTH_*` line.

**Open:** authorization codes are written to the nginx access log (and same-origin Referer). The two real codes from 2026-10-04 were never exchanged and are long expired. A dedicated callback path with `access_log off` needs a new redirect URI on the Google client, a backend route and an nginx restart — not done (out of scope: no restart, no Google console change).

**Safety:** no email, draft, Gmail call, restart, migration or credential change.

## 2026-10-06 — Email Agent: 25-message live read-only sample; four classifier/policy defects found (not patched)

Ran the unchanged CLI (`run-once --limit 25 --dry-run`) in a one-off process with `EMAIL_AGENT_QUERY="in:inbox -from:me newer_than:30d"` set for that process only (the setting already existed; no code change, default query untouched).

**Result:** 25 listed, 25 processed, 0 failed. Categories: shipping_eurosender 12, supplier 9, newsletter_marketing 2, account_security 1, payment_billing 1. Context: supplier resolved 9; customer / order / shipment resolved 0. Policy: human 12, safe-for-future-automation 9, no-reply 4. Gmail requests GET-only (1 list, 25 thread reads, 1 profile); labels of all 34 messages in those threads unchanged on re-read; `email_agent_messages` absent before and after; alembic 0038; no restart.

**Sample composition:** no customer mail. The 25 newest inbound messages were Eurosender (mostly sandbox order notices), supplier marketing mail, two social newsletters, one Google alert, one vendor receipt. The 30-day window holds at least 100 more inbound messages from other senders (ids counted only, not read), so customer/order paths remain unexercised on live mail.

**Defects (VERIFIED on the live sample, root cause in code, NOT fixed in this run):**
1. **Supplier newsletters classified as supplier business mail and given a reply draft.** All 9 `supplier` messages (ASAP Network 7, SNG Barratt 2) carry `List-Unsubscribe` (7 also `List-Id`, 2 `Precedence: bulk`). `classifier.classify` only checks bulk/automated headers when neither supplier nor customer is resolved, so a known supplier's marketing blast becomes `supplier` → `draft_supplier_ack`. Fix: evaluate bulk/automated headers before the resolved-supplier branch (keep the supplier reference; category `newsletter_marketing` / `automated_notification`).
2. **Inactive supplier treated as verified.** ASAP Network is `is_active=false` (`account_active_pending_brand_approval`) yet resolves and qualifies for an acknowledgement. Fix: `policy.decide` requires `supplier.is_active` for `draft_supplier_ack`, else human.
3. **Boilerplate triggers risk flags.** All 9 Eurosender sandbox order notices were flagged `cancellation` + `price_change` ("cancel" in the footer, "discount" in a promo line) and escalated to a human; 9 of the 12 escalations are this noise. Fix: for notification categories, take serious flags from the subject and the opening of the body only, not the whole text.
4. **Gmail quota 403 handled as a permanent "scope" error.** Follow-up verification reads hit `Quota exceeded … Units per minute per user`; `gmail_client._call` maps every 403 to `kind="scope"` (non-retryable, aborts the cycle, would alert the owner). Same root cause as the known API-disabled mislabel. Fix: read the error reason — rate/quota → `transient`, API disabled → `config`, insufficient scope → `scope` — and pace thread reads.

**Correct behaviour confirmed:** the 5 Eurosender order codes in the subjects match 0 orders (no order in the DB has any Eurosender code — they are sandbox test shipments), so "order unresolved" is right; no identifier was cited without DB verification.

**Tests:** 112 passed, 1 skipped. No code changed.

## 2026-10-06 — Email Agent: the four live-sample defects root-fixed and re-verified live (read-only)

**1. Supplier newsletters treated as supplier business mail.** Root cause: `classifier.classify` evaluated bulk / automated headers only when neither supplier nor customer was resolved. Fix: explicit precedence — auto-reply headers → `automated_notification` for any sender; bulk headers (`List-Unsubscribe`, `List-Id`, `Precedence: bulk`) → `newsletter_marketing` even for a known supplier; a resolved customer is never dropped as a newsletter (classified by content, flagged `bulk_headers` → human); a no-reply address alone is a weak signal (known supplier stays `supplier`, flagged `automated_sender` → human).

**2. Inactive supplier qualified for automation.** Root cause: `policy.decide` checked only that a supplier row matched. Fix: `draft_supplier_ack` requires `supplier.is_active is True` (missing / null = not active); `drafts.build_draft` refuses otherwise. Domain matching unchanged.

**3. Footer / order-summary words raised risk flags.** Root cause: risk keywords were searched in the whole body. Live templates showed "cancel" in a 1,645-character legal paragraph and "discount" in a price-table row ("User credit discount"). Fix: `normalize.meaningful_text` — automated notices use subject + opening up to the sign-off / first footer line (max 1,500 chars); human mail uses the full text minus boilerplate lines, keeps text after a sign-off and keeps first-person lines. Also found while writing the tests: `cancelled / canceled / refunded` did not match the keyword `cancel` / `refund` (word-boundary match) — added; and `price_change` / `address_change` now escalate when they appear in a notice's meaningful text.

**4. Every Gmail 403 reported as "scope".** Root cause: `gmail_client._call` mapped status 403 to `scope`. Fix: `classify_error` reads `error.errors[].reason`, `error.details[].reason` and the message → `rate_limit` / `config` (API disabled) / `scope` / `auth` / `permission` / `unknown` / `transient` / `permanent`. Only `rate_limit` and `transient` are retried in the call (rate limit backs off 5 s, 15 s). In a cycle, `rate_limit` releases the claim without using an attempt and ends the cycle as `throttled` (no owner alert); `auth / scope / config / permission` abort and alert. Pacing: 1.5 s between Gmail calls (`EMAIL_AGENT_MIN_REQUEST_INTERVAL_MS`); a thread is read once per cycle. Quota evidence: the project's per-user limit is 6,000 units/minute (read in the Cloud console; it was 15,000) and ~75 thread reads in a minute exhausted it.

**Tests:** 33 new tests failed against the old code (reproduction) and pass now. `tests/test_email_agent.py` + `tests/test_gmail_oauth_setup.py`: 155 passed, 1 skipped; with the real-Postgres store test: 146 passed in `test_email_agent.py`. App-import suites (`test_overnight_schedule`, `test_harvest_supervisor_persistence`, `test_db_credentials`, `test_docker_build_context`): 58 passed.

**Live re-verification (one-off process, dry-run, GET only, paced):**
- Run A, same query as the defective sample (`in:inbox -from:me newer_than:30d`, 25 messages): before → after — `supplier` 9 → 0 and `newsletter_marketing` 2 → 11 (all 9 supplier mails carry bulk headers); safe-for-automation 9 → 0; human 12 → 2 (Google security alert, vendor receipt); Eurosender notices with flags 10 → 0. No quota error in 49 thread reads.
- Run B, `in:inbox -from:me newer_than:30d -category:promotions -category:social -category:updates` (Gmail accepted the category filters; the window holds 18 such messages): 15 Eurosender sandbox notices → no flags, `log_only`; 1 Eurosender password-recovery notice → `security` → human (a genuine serious topic still escalates); 1 manually written reply from SNG Barratt (active supplier, no bulk headers) → `supplier`, safe tier; 1 vendor sales follow-up → `unknown` → human. No customer mail exists in that window.
- Both runs: zero non-GET Gmail requests, labels of every message unchanged on re-read, `email_agent_messages` absent, alembic 0038, no restart. A live quota error did not occur after the fix, so the rate-limit path is proven by tests using Google's real error text, not by a live event.

## 2026-10-06 — Email Agent: two compose pass-through gaps closed; heartbeat test row still present

**Root cause:** `docker-compose.yml` injects into the backend only the variables listed under the service's `environment:`; `.env` is used for `${...}` interpolation, not as an `env_file`. `EMAIL_AGENT_QUERY` and `EMAIL_AGENT_MAX_ATTEMPTS` were added to `email_agent/config.py` without matching lines, so a value in `.env` could never reach the container.

**Findings (not patched in this run):**
1. **The replies carried no customer text.** Each reply body is only dots above Outlook's quoted original, so the "customer request" lives in the quote of OUR outbound message. Consequences: classification rested on the subject alone ("order" in the test label → `order_shipping` for A/B/C; D and E → `unknown`), and E reached a human because the category was unknown, not because the address / email / phone change was detected (`risk_flags` empty). Proposed fix: when the new text has no letters or digits after separators are stripped, flag `empty_message` and route to a human.
3. **Order identifiers are taken from quoted text by design.** `context.resolve_context` reads candidate tokens from the full body, including the quote; ownership is still enforced. Kept as is unless the owner wants quoted identifiers ignored (a customer replying to an order confirmation with "where is it?" depends on this).
4. **Outlook's reply separator survives quote stripping (normalization, cosmetic).** The `________________________________` line stays in `new_text`. The `From: / Sent: / To: / Subject:` block is cut correctly; sender, order selection and risk flags were not affected.

## 2026-10-09 — Email Agent: a reply with no newly-authored text can no longer reach the safe tier

**Reported by the 2026-10-08 live E2E:** two real customer replies whose own text was only dots above Outlook's quoted original were placed in `safe_for_future_automation` (`draft_order_status`).

**Root cause (three places, one idea — nothing checked that the sender had written anything):**
1. `classifier.classify` built its text as `subject + (new_text or body_text)`. With dots as new text the category came from the inherited `Re:` subject; with an empty new text it fell back to the FULL body, i.e. the quoted original.
2. `classifier.detect_flags` used the same `new_text or body_text` fallback, so risk words could be lifted from the quote.
3. `policy.decide` had no rule about an empty message; a verified order (resolved from the quoted order number) plus an `order_shipping` category was enough for the safe tier.

**Fix:**
- `normalize.authored_text()` = the text above the quote, boilerplate lines removed, never falling back to the quote; `normalize.has_meaningful_text()` = at least two letters or digits in any script (whitespace, punctuation, dots, divider lines are empty). `strip_quoted` now drops the mail client's trailing divider line (Outlook's row of underscores).
- `classifier.detect_flags`: a human (non-notification) message without meaningful authored text gets `empty_message`; for human mail, flags are computed on the authored text only.
- `classifier.classify`: content keywords come from the subject + authored text only; an empty message contributes none (the customer's own earlier inbound messages may still set the category), otherwise `unknown` with reason "no newly-authored text".
- `policy.decide`: `empty_message` is checked before the category and always returns `human_approval_required`; it is also in `HUMAN_FLAGS`. `drafts.build_draft` refuses a source email with no authored text.
- Unchanged on purpose: `context.resolve_context` still reads identifiers from the quoted text (ownership enforced).

**Tests:** 30 focused tests (23 failed on the old code): empty / whitespace / punctuation / dots / divider-only replies over Outlook- and Gmail-style quotes, quote-only, real short replies in English, Hebrew and Arabic, real reply + quoted order number still safe, empty reply + quoted valid order → order resolved but human, quoted risk words not lifted. Email Agent + OAuth + compose suites: 184 passed, 3 skipped (with the real-Postgres store test). App-import / config suites: 58 passed; host compose test 3/3.

**Live replay (read-only, in memory, GET only):** the same two real replies now give — order still resolved (`AUTO-2026-BC7D3824`, `AUTO-2026-1D2E937B`), `risk_flags=['empty_message']`, `human_approval_required`, no reply text. Gmail: 5 GET, 0 non-GET. Backend `RestartCount=0`; the fix is on disk only (not loaded in the running app); agent still disabled.

## 2026-10-09 — Email Agent: terse "change address" was not recognised as an address change (live message)

**Live check (read-only, in memory):** one new direct message from the owner's registered customer address, Gmail id `1a11d8f078c0eda3`, subject `AUTO-2026-BC7D3824`, body `change address`, no quote. Customer resolved, order `AUTO-2026-BC7D3824` resolved and confirmed owned by the sender, no shipment, `human_approval_required`, no reply text. But `risk_flags` was empty and the category `unknown`: it reached a human only because nothing matched.

**Root cause:** `classifier._FLAGS["address_change"]` was a list of whole phrases ("change my address", "change the address", "new address", ...). The real wording "change address" matched none. Requests to change an account's email / phone had no detector at all.

**Fix:** `classifier._FLAG_PATTERNS` detects sensitive changes by structure — a change verb next to the thing being changed, in English, Hebrew and Arabic — in addition to the phrase list. `address_change` (verb + address, "address is wrong", "different address", ...) and a new flag `account_change` (verb + email / phone / mobile). Fillers are restricted to determiners so "update me by email" or "what is your address?" do not match. Category: an address change is `order_shipping`; an account-contact change is `account_security`. Both flags are in `policy.HUMAN_FLAGS` and `SERIOUS_FLAGS`, so they escalate in human mail and in notices. Detection runs on the authored text only (unchanged rule from `b1bc40d`): a quoted address change is not the customer's request.

**Tests:** 40 focused tests (28 failed on the old code): the live message shape, 18 address-change wordings and 10 contact-change wordings in three languages, 9 ordinary sentences that must not be flagged, quoted vs authored, a notice whose opening reports an address change. Email Agent + OAuth + compose: 224 passed, 3 skipped (with the real-Postgres store test). App-import / config suites: 58 passed; host compose test 3/3.

**Live replay of the same message after the fix:** `order_shipping` (0.70, "content signals in this message: address_change"), `risk_flags=['address_change']`, policy `human_approval_required` with reason `risk flags: address_change`, no reply text, not sendable. Gmail: GET only (first run 5 GET, replay 3 GET, 0 non-GET); labels unchanged (`INBOX`, `UNREAD`); business tables and the order's stored address unchanged; `email_agent_messages` absent; alembic 0038; backend `RestartCount=0`, agent disabled, fix on disk only.

**Remaining gap:** only one real sensitive-change wording has been seen live; the patterns are tested against written examples, not a corpus of real customer mail.

**Run:** the 12 requested scenarios (status, not received, tracking, wrong part, cancellation, refund, address change, email/phone change, status above a quoted address change, empty reply with the order only in the quote, another customer's order, nonexistent order) through the real pipeline (`agent.process_message`), real `DbContextSource` (SELECT only) and an in-memory store; the Gmail side was an in-process transport serving messages shaped like the real Hotmail ones. **Defects found and fixed:**
1. **"My order has not arrived" → automatic "it is delivered".** No flag covered a non-delivery / delay / loss claim, and the word "order" made it `order_shipping` → `draft_order_status`. On a delivered order that reply contradicts the customer.

## 2026-10-09 — Email Agent: live run on 17 real Hotmail test messages; three defects found and fixed

**Run:** the owner sent 17 test messages from `khalilayoub23@hotmail.com` (05:55–06:03 UTC, Gmail ids `1a11f3b8…` to `1a11f421…`). Exactly those 17 were processed with the unchanged pipeline in a one-off process (`agent.process_message`, in-memory store, real `DbContextSource`). Each was checked to come from the expected sender and not carry the SENT label before processing.

**Defects (all VERIFIED on the live messages):**
1. **Mis-decoded text (normalization).** Gmail's API returns text parts as UTF-8, but Hotmail labels them `charset="Windows-1252"` / `iso-8859-1`. `normalize._decode_part` trusted the label, so `“Where is my order?”` became `â€œWhere is my order?â€�`; Hebrew or Arabic sent the same way would have been garbled. Fix: strict UTF-8 first, the declared charset only for bytes that are not valid UTF-8.
2. **Typographic apostrophe hid a claim (classification).** `“My order hasn’t arrived yet.”` raised no `delivery_problem` flag (keyword `hasn't arrived` is ASCII) and reached the safe tier with an automatic "status" reply. Fix: `classifier.fold()` maps typographic quotes / apostrophes to ASCII before keyword matching.
3. **Second order reference ignored (context).** Subject = the customer's own order, body = "i want to check for my friend order AUTO-2026-BC7D3857" (that number does not exist). The agent resolved the subject's order and prepared that order's status. Fix: `context.resolve_context` marks the order `ambiguous` (details withheld → human) when the sender's own words cite another reference of the same shape as the resolved order (same prefix up to the last `-`, same length) that matches no order.

**Tests:** 9 focused (7 failed on the old code), built from the exact live bytes. Email Agent + OAuth + compose: 263 passed, 3 skipped (with the real-Postgres store test).

**After the fix, same 17 messages:** status questions (2) and the tracking request → safe tier, order `AUTO-2026-BC7D3824` resolved and owned, no tracking quoted (no verified carrier record). Not-arrived → `delivery_problem`, human. Wrong part → `complaint_dispute`, human. Cancel, refund → human. Address change (3 messages, including "Change address." only in the subject) → `address_change`, human. Email/phone change (2) → `account_change`, human. Empty bodies (3) → `empty_message`, human. Order number only, no request → `unknown`, human. Friend's order → `ambiguous`, human. Gmail: 39 GET per run, 0 non-GET; labels of all 17 unchanged; business tables unchanged (orders, users, returns, payments); `email_agent_messages` absent; alembic 0038; backend `RestartCount=0`, agent disabled.

**Not covered live** (no such message was sent): a reply with authored text above a quoted original (scenario i), an empty reply with the order only in the quote (j), another customer's existing order (k). All three pass in the offline matrix with real DB context (`AUTO-2026-43EA94CF`, owned by the test account `test@autosparefinder.com`, for k).

## 2026-10-09 — Email Agent: thread context limited to explicit replies (live same-subject threading)

**Live scenarios i, j, k:** NOT run — BLOCKED. No new message from the test sender arrived after the 17 processed earlier (searched 06:10 UTC: 17 messages since 2026-10-09, none a reply, none citing `AUTO-2026-43EA94CF`). Offline results are not substituted for them.

**Defect (VERIFIED on live messages):** Gmail grouped independent emails that merely share a subject into one thread (13 messages titled `AUTO-2026-BC7D3824`; 2 titled `“Change address.”`), with no `In-Reply-To` / `References` linking them. `context.resolve_context` took order tokens from EVERY inbound message in the thread, and `classifier.classify` took its category fallback from them. Live consequences: message `1a11f3e7f457e401` ("Change address.", no order number) resolved `AUTO-2026-BC7D3824` from a separate email in its thread (`1a11f3efec23b465`); the empty-body messages `1a11f40a911581b3` and `1a11f410122d5209` took the category `order_shipping` from unrelated emails.

**Fix:** `normalize.associated_messages()` — the thread messages whose Message-ID the current message names in `In-Reply-To` / `References`. Context tokens and the category fallback use only the current message (subject, authored text, its own quote) plus those associated messages. Combined with the earlier same-shape stray-reference rule, a valid order in another message can neither stand in for nor disambiguate the current message's order reference. Documented in `docs/EMAIL_AGENT.md`.

Two existing follow-up tests now carry real reply headers. Email Agent + OAuth + compose: 270 passed, 3 skipped (with the real-Postgres store test).

## 2026-10-09 — OAuth values in nginx logs: root cause, fix (staged, not deployed), deployment runbook

**Root cause (VERIFIED, counts only):** `deploy/nginx.conf` had no `log_format`, so nginx used "combined" and logged the full request line and Referer. A Google OAuth redirect to `/?state=..&code=..` therefore wrote the code (a) in the request line (5 lines in the current container log), (b) in the Referer of every follow-up request from that page (24 lines: assets, `/api/v1/parts/categories`, `/chat`), and (c) in the error log's `referrer:` field for missing static files (2 lines, `car.svg`). No access / refresh / ID tokens appear in any log. All codes found are expired or already exchanged.

**Fix (`deploy/nginx.conf`, additive; the owner's uncommitted resolver edit is untouched):** chained `map`s produce `$request_redacted` and `$http_referer_redacted` with `code`, `state`, `access_token`, `refresh_token`, `id_token` values replaced by `<redacted>`; `log_format redacted` (combined fields) + `access_log … redacted`; http-level `log_not_found off` (the error log cannot be formatted and copied the raw Referer); `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` on `location /` responses to a request carrying `code`. `maintenance/gmail_oauth_setup.py` now recognises `code=<redacted>` (reports `code_redacted`, refuses to exchange, asks for `--code`).

**Tests:** host test `backend/tests/test_nginx_oauth_log_redaction.py` 5/5 — it runs the real nginx.conf in a throwaway container (no network, read-only mounts) and proves the fake code / state / token never reach either log, the 404 and the request path stay visible, and the landing response carries `no-referrer`; against the pre-fix config 4 of 5 fail. Helper test added (10 passed). Email Agent + OAuth + compose: 273 passed, 3 skipped. Host compose test 3/3; existing `test_nginx_upstream.py` passes; `docker compose config` valid; `nginx -t` successful; app-import suites 58 passed.

**Not deployed:** nginx needs `docker restart autospare_nginx`. Runbook for nginx, backend recreate + migration 0039, read-only verification, activation and rollback: `docs/EMAIL_AGENT.md` § Deployment runbook. Nothing restarted, migrated or committed.

## 2026-10-09 — nginx OAuth log redaction ACTIVATED (Phase 1, nginx only)

**APPLIED** to `autospare_nginx` (owner-approved `docker restart autospare_nginx`; container id `4a157de882c6`, image unchanged, nginx 1.31.1). Preflight: the mounted file was byte-identical to the tested one; `nginx -t` passed with the production binary; the harvester was idle (queue drained, resting) so no relay post went through nginx during the restart.

**Defect found by the first live check and fixed before closing:** the first activation (06:44 UTC) redacted `code` and `state` but, when a URL carried `access_token`, `refresh_token` and `id_token` together, only one of them — a single map used an alternation and replaces one match. The leaked values were synthetic test strings. Fix: one map per parameter (`$oauth_rq_1..5`, `$oauth_rf_1..5`) plus a final guard that withholds the whole query ("`?<query withheld>`", rebuilt from the original request line so the real path is kept) if any sensitive value is still unredacted, e.g. a repeated parameter. The host test now covers multi-token and duplicate-parameter URLs (5/5 pass; on the first-activation config the multi-token case fails). Re-validated with the production binary, then activated with a second `docker restart autospare_nginx` (06:46:05 UTC, healthy after 11 s).

**Verified live after the second restart (synthetic values only):** inside nginx and through the public domain, `/?state=..&code=..` is logged as `state=<redacted>&...&code=<redacted>` with path, status and the non-sensitive `iss` / `scope` kept; a 404 with an OAuth Referer is logged with the Referer redacted and produces no error-log line; three tokens in one URL → all `<redacted>`; a repeated `code` → `GET /?<query withheld>`; `/plain-check?lang=he` logged unchanged. 0 synthetic secret values in any log line. Responses to `?code=` carry `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, others `strict-origin-when-cross-origin`. Public `/` and `/api/v1/system/health` return 200.

**Untouched (ids and start times identical before and after):** backend (`68be62378617`, started 2026-10-04 17:20 UTC, harvester pid unchanged), frontend, whatsapp_bridge, postgres_pii, postgres_catalog. ### 2026-10-09 — Startup 403s root-caused; startup no longer waits for the optional warm-up; Email Agent runtime kill switch

**Status: code + tests APPLIED on disk; NOT DEPLOYED** (uvicorn still runs the code loaded at 06:58:14Z; the bind-mounted CLI already runs the new code). No restart, no DB write, no Gmail call, agent still disabled.

**Startup 403s — root cause (VERIFIED from the 06:58 start logs + code).** `_warm_search_paths` calls `search_parts(..., redis=None)`. For a non-empty query `search_parts` always started `_fetch_ext_suppliers`, a background lookup against every external supplier whose ONLY output is the Redis entry `ext_sup:<query>` — skipped when `redis` is None. So each start sent 5 queries × (PartSouq, Autodoc, Amayama → HTTP 403, server IP blocked) + 5 eBay Browse API calls + 1 eBay token request, and discarded every answer. Bounded already (one request per supplier, `wait_for` 2 s, no retry, exceptions swallowed); not customer-facing (a 403 yields `[]` or a price-0 placeholder that `_sanitize_external_offer` drops); not fatal. The same waste happened on every `search_parts` caller that passes `redis=None` (`routes/parts.py` ~2634 and ~3541, `maintenance/run_fitment_step1_parity_check.py`).
- Fix: `routes/parts.py::_should_fetch_external_suppliers(query, redis)` — the lookup runs only with a query AND a Redis client to cache into. Customer requests (real Redis client) are unchanged.
- **Second defect found:** startup `await`ed `_warm_search_paths()` before "Application startup complete", although its comment called it background. Cases allow up to 12 + 4×25 + 120 s ≈ 230 s cold, all on the API/health-check readiness path. Now `asyncio.create_task(_guarded_task(...))` with a strong reference (`_SEARCH_WARMUP_TASK`).
- Warm-up results are now classified: new `search_warmup.py` (`run_warmup_cases` → ok / timeout / error per case, exception type logged, never raises; `summary_line` → `primed X/N (timeouts=, errors=)` instead of an unconditional "primed 6").
- Not changed (needs a production config decision): live customer searches still send one request per new query to the three blocked sites. `EXTERNAL_ENABLE_PARTSOUQ/AUTODOC/AMAYAMA=0` would stop that (env change + recreation → owner approval).

**Email Agent kill switch.** `EMAIL_AGENT_ENABLED` needs a recreation to change; there was no runtime stop. New `email_agent/control.py`: state file `/app/state/email_agent_control.json` (worker_state volume, shared by the uvicorn loop and `docker exec` CLI; `EMAIL_AGENT_CONTROL_FILE` overrides). Runs only when the file is valid JSON with `{"mode":"run"}`; missing → halted `not_armed` (default); unreadable / invalid / unknown mode / >4 KB → halted (fail closed). Atomic writes (temp + `os.replace`). Checkpoints: loop each iteration (no Gmail client / heartbeat / DB while halted, re-check 60 s); `process_once` start (no token refresh, no Gmail call, no store write); before each claim; before the draft step; before saving a result (both paths); `GmailClient._call` immediately before any non-GET request; CLI `run-once` (incl. `--dry-run`) exits 3 without building a client. A halt mid-message releases the claim (status `retry`, attempt not consumed). CLI `control` / `halt` / `arm`; status endpoint and CLI `status` report it. Check cost measured in the container: 17 µs (no file) / 45 µs (armed). Worst-case halt latency for reads = one in-flight Gmail GET (≈95 s with retries); a draft POST is checked immediately before it is sent. Remaining races documented in `docs/EMAIL_AGENT.md` § Runtime kill switch (µs window before an already-guarded POST; a halt between the two draft checks escalates that one message to a human; `release` is the one store write after a halt). Sending stays impossible by construction.

### 2026-10-10 — Final pre-deployment gate: startup warm-up + Email Agent kill switch (code and tests only)

**Status: PASS as a code-and-test gate. NOT DEPLOYED** — uvicorn still runs the code loaded 2026-10-09 06:58:14Z. No container recreated, no agent activation, no draft, no supplier config change, no production DB write, no commit.

**Kill switch — paths traced (grep, 2026-10-10).** Entry points that process mail: the supervised loop (`BACKEND_API_ROUTES.py:2816-2817` → `email_agent/loop.py`) and CLI `run-once`. One route, read-only (`routes/email_agent_routes.py`). Exactly one Gmail write: `POST /drafts` (`gmail_client.py::create_draft`); no send method, six-endpoint allowlist unchanged. Store writes: `claim`, `mark_draft_attempt`, `save_result`, `mark_failed`, `release`.

**Race assessment.** "Prevents new writes after halt" and "cancels an in-flight request" are different guarantees; only the first is claimed — a sent HTTP request cannot be recalled. The first is now exact without holding a lock across the network call: new `control.write_intent` — the writer records a marker, THEN reads the control, sends, removes the marker; `set_mode(halt)` writes the control, THEN reads the markers. So for every write either the writer saw the halt (nothing sent) or `halt` lists it in `writes_in_flight`. `halt` printing `[]` = nothing in flight and nothing will start. A listed write completes within the 25 s transport timeout (POST never retried). A lock held across the request was rejected (a hung request or crashed holder would block the kill switch). Also changed: a halted write is refused before the token step (no network at all); the intent fails closed if its marker cannot be written; a result is always saved when a Gmail draft was already created (never an untracked draft). Remaining limits (docs/EMAIL_AGENT.md § Runtime kill switch): listed writes complete; a killed process leaves a marker reported `stale` after 180 s; halt between the two draft checks escalates that message to a human; local bookkeeping rows (`release`, `save_result` of an existing draft, `mark_failed`) are still written; an in-flight GET completes (≈95 s worst case); the control file is protected only by container file access.

## 2026-10-27 — LLM provider switch: HF Router (DeepInfra) primary, Groq fallback, Cerebras off

- **Why:** recurring Cerebras 429s; owner research + live HF price check. Live `router.huggingface.co/v1/models` (2026-10-27): gpt-oss-120b on DeepInfra $0.037 in / $0.17 out per 1M vs Cerebras $0.35 / $0.75. gpt-oss-20b on DeepInfra $0.03 / $0.14. Owner chose 120B (same model as before) on DeepInfra as primary.
- **Change:** `hf_client.py` — `_hf_primary_text()` runs first in `hf_text` for gpt-oss models (`openai/gpt-oss-120b:deepinfra`); returns reply `content` only (never `reasoning` → no CoT leak); 5-min cooldown on 401/402/403/429. `CEREBRAS_ENABLED=0` → on HF failure go to Groq gpt-oss-120b → `GROQ_MODEL`. Env: `LLM_PRIMARY_PROVIDER` (hf|cerebras), `HF_PRIMARY_PROVIDER` (deepinfra), `CEREBRAS_ENABLED` — in `.env` and `docker-compose.yml`. `CEREBRAS_API_KEY` deliberately kept: `BACKEND_AI_AGENTS` returns mocked/offline replies when it is unset.
- **Verified live (in container):** Hebrew + Arabic replies via DeepInfra 200; forced HF failure → Groq 200; 0 Cerebras calls after deploy. Tool-call test (Arabic) returned a valid `search_parts` call.
- **Known trade-offs:** DeepInfra latency 5–12 s per reply (Groq ~0.3 s, Cerebras was fast). HF account `autospare` (PRO) has $2.00 credit, auto-recharge OFF — when it runs out HF returns 402 and traffic falls to Groq (free tier, can 429) until credits are added.

## 2026-10-27 — Fabricated shipping range, policy enforcement outside the model, reply language — ROOT FIX (branch `fix/reply-language`, NOT deployed)

**STATUS:** owner approved deploy + live DeepInfra check + HF alert + HF credit (2026-10-27 ~11:30 Israel). Deploy and
credit purchase recorded in the deploy entry below.

### A. Fabricated "shipping ₪29–₪149"
- **Premise corrected (verified):** Eurosender was never the customer-facing shipping-price source. `EurosenderAdapter.get_quote`
  is reached only from post-payment fulfillment (`eurosender_fulfillment` → `evaluate_and_create_shipment`), gated by
  `EUROSENDER_SUPPLIER_ALLOWLIST`, which is EMPTY in production (read 2026-10-27: len 0, ENABLED=1, SANDBOX=0) → no supplier
  is routed, no quote is shown to customers. The customer shipping figure is the per-offer `shipping` inside the canonical
  price (`calculate_customer_price_from_ils` / `_customer_price_fields` → `customer_total_ils`), i.e. what checkout charges.
  Wiring live Eurosender quotes into chat would be a new production integration — out of scope, not done.
- **Root cause:** the range was HARD-CODED (since 2026-03-20/21, `5ac4f5c` "shipping range in NIR prompts"): SalesAgent prompt
  ("Always show … מע\"מ 18% + משלוח ₪29–₪149"), ServiceAgent prompt (same, flat 18% VAT too — wrong for foreign suppliers),
  and four catalog-context templates (`"₪29-149 משלוח (לפי ספק)"`) although each offer's real `shipping` was in the dict.
  The 2026-07-11 shipping-truth fix removed fictional supplier rates but missed these copies. Also invented delivery
  windows: `estimated_delivery_days or 14` / `"10-14 ימים"` presented as fact; brain list labelled totals "incl. VAT"
  although they include shipping.
- **Fix:** templates show the offer's real figure (`_shipping_fact_he`) or "shown at checkout"; prompts: only figures in the
  data, VAT exactly as given; SHIPPING TRUTH gains "no range, no typical/starting-from amount"; `delivery_days_confirmed`
  flag + `_delivery_fact_he` / localized "delivery time shown at checkout"; label "incl. VAT and shipping"; and the
  application-level guard below blocks any ungrounded amount (both ends of a range) on every customer agent/channel.
- **Before/after (live, Groq):** before `"עלות המשלוח נעה בין 29 ₪ ל‑149 ₪"`, `"Shipping is ₪29–₪149 (NIS)…"`; after (3/3, en/he/ar)
  "the exact amount appears at checkout", no amount, policy=ok.

### B. Policy enforcement (outside the model) — new `backend/policy_guard.py`
1. **Groq truncation (policy loss):** `groq_text` cut system prompts to 5,000 chars (customer prompts 9.5–14K) → PROHIBITED,
   SHIPPING TRUTH, VERIFY, LANGUAGE and the reply-language block dropped on every Groq fallback; prompt cut to 6,000 → current
   message lost. **Verified limit:** `x-ratelimit-limit-tokens: 8000`; 13,120-char prompt = 3,149 tokens, HTTP 200.
   **Fix:** `fit_request` with `GROQ_MAX_REQUEST_TOKENS=8000` − 1000 completion − 300 margin: shortens only
   `[GUIDANCE]` blocks (SALES FLOW, PROFESSIONAL SKILLS), then oldest history; mandatory policy + current message never cut;
   otherwise `PolicyBudgetExceeded` → localized safe reply. DeepInfra/Gemini/Cerebras paths receive the full system (no cut).
2. **Ungrounded business claims:** `BaseAgent.think` validates every customer reply: each currency amount (incl. ranges) and
   each link must appear in the turn's application data (agent prompt suffix = catalog/order context) or the customer's own
   messages; static prompt text is NOT grounding. One bounded corrective retry, then localized fallback; `[ReplyLang] …
   policy=` log with provider. Payment/order links only from data; own static pages allowed.
3. **Router permission bypass:** "admin only" was prompt wording; `route()` returned the model's choice unchecked → customers
   could reach `social_media_manager_agent` (campaign plans/post drafts), `supplier_manager_agent`, `tech_agent` (signature
   mismatch → crash). **Fix:** `RouterAgent._enforce_route` — customer channels limited to `policy_guard.CUSTOMER_AGENTS`
   (7); unknown/internal → service_agent, `route_blocked_from` recorded.
4. **Editor:** `_format_response_for_customer` rewrite rejected if it changes language or adds numbers/links.
5. **Autonomous NOA public replies:** `noa_ops.send_page_reply(actor="autonomous")` also runs the grounded-claims gate
   (no amounts/foreign links without data) → stays pending for the owner. Production runs AUTOREPLY=0 (owner approves).
6. **Tools:** no model-driven tool execution exists — `think()` never forwards `tools`; consequential actions (checkout link,
   orders, payments) are deterministic code paths. Tested.

### C. Reply language (from the earlier entry, integrated)
Six causes: conflicting prompts ("Default Hebrew", "ALWAYS respond in Hebrew"), first-message rule, brain language never
passed to agents, editor without English rule reading the previous message, Hebrew-only fixed texts (timeouts = the identical
OrdersAgent replies; "wrong part"/"frustrated" canned answers), Groq truncation. Fix: `reply_language.py` + per-turn context
var + enforcement in `BaseAgent.think`; empty reply = failure. Registry: **11 agents** (7 customer-facing + router + 3 internal).

## 2026-10-27 — Shipping is INCLUDED in every price and charged ONCE (web-cart double charge, chat price, cart page, agents' wording) — DEPLOYED 13:23 Israel

- **Owner:** agents told customers shipping "appears at checkout / after payment" — wrong and dangerous ("we must not charge
  the client twice"); suppliers' shipping fees are known and added to the part price.
- **Rule (one, everywhere):** total = cost×1.45 + conditional VAT + that offer's delivery fee
  (`resolve_customer_shipping_fee`: supplier shipping, else supplier profile), counted ONCE, never marked up.
  Canonical: `routes/parts._customer_price_fields` (search/compare) and `create_whatsapp_checkout` already did this.
- **Root causes found (verified in code + live data: 915,293 of 1,519,166 available priced offers carry supplier shipping):**
  1. `routes/orders.create_order` (web cart charge): unit price = (cost + supplier shipping)×1.45 AND a separate per-supplier
     fee (`get_supplier_shipping`, ₪59 default) → shipping charged twice. Before/after on a disposable DB (same 2 items):
     deployed code subtotal ₪333.50, fixed ₪217.50 (+ VAT + one ₪45 fee). Historical web orders with such items: 3
     (2026-04-17, ₪152.01 each: 1 confirmed, 1 delivered, 1 pending) — whether they were overcharged is UNVERIFIED (owner).
  2. `BaseAgent.calculate_customer_price_from_ils` (chat search + `routes/parts` identify + `routes/brands` pages, 8 call
     sites) put supplier shipping into the margin base AND as the delivery fee; 4 USD call sites added `shipping_cost_usd`
     into the cost. Fixed at the helper (shipping never in the margin base) + the 4 call sites; USD helper too.
  3. Web cart page/store: the cart API price already INCLUDES VAT (`_customer_unit_price`, since 2026-09-21) but the page
     added 18% again (store: flat 18% on every item) and showed an invented ₪91 when no shipping field was sent.
  4. Wording: SHIPPING TRUTH said "a per-supplier fee shown at checkout"; templates/labels said "יוצג בקופה".
- **Fix:** `routes/orders._order_line_pricing` (same rule as checkout/search; one fee per supplier = max); helper fix;
  cart API adds `vatIncluded`, `deliveryFee` (per line), `shippingCost` (once per supplier); frontend
  `utils/cartTotals.js` shared by store + Cart page (VAT shown as contained, delivery once per supplier, no fallback fee);
  SHIPPING TRUTH rewritten (included, charged once, never "at checkout/after payment"); fixed texts; `policy_guard`
  violation `shipping_deferred` (he/ar/en, cost phrase deferred to checkout/payment in the same sentence) → one corrective
  retry → localized fallback.
- **Eurosender (re-verified):** used only in post-payment fulfillment, `EUROSENDER_SUPPLIER_ALLOWLIST` empty — it does not
  price customer shipping; supplier shipping (`supplier_parts.shipping_cost_ils`, e.g. Sendcloud/eBay/RockAuto sync) does.
- **Tests:** `test_shipping_included.py` (parity of every path, cart API, guard, agent correction in 3 languages);
  `test_order_shipping_e2e.py` (real `create_order` on a disposable DB; FAILS on the deployed code: ₪333.50 vs ₪217.50);
  frontend cart math 6/6 (Node, real `cartTotals.js`); frontend test build OK. Updated: `test_cart_vat` (VAT contained),
  three earlier tests that asserted the old "shown at checkout" wording. Suites: 560 passed (language/policy/shipping);
  broad regression identical to the deployed baseline except those intended updates; DB E2E: customer flow 33/33,
  checkout-idempotency + side-effects + WhatsApp late-reply 33/33.
- **Deploy:** backend recreated 13:22 (preflight SAFE), frontend image rebuilt + recreated 13:23 Israel, both healthy.
- **Live verification:** public site serves the new Cart chunk (deliveryFee present, 0 × `||91`); 3 real offers with
  supplier shipping: order = search = chat total (e.g. cost ₪72.31 + ship ₪114.17 → ₪219.02; old order math ≈ ₪384.57);
  cart API returns price (VAT incl.) + deliveryFee + shippingCost; live chat 4/4 (ar/he/en + "is shipping charged
  separately after I pay?") answer "delivery is included in each part's price, not a separate charge".
