### WS1 — Which owner_console.py the process is running — **PASS (production VERIFIED)**
- **Root cause:** CPython compiles a module once and does not re-read the source, so the hash of the file on disk proves nothing about the running process. There was no introspection path (no py-spy/gdb, ptrace restricted, a static `/version`). Also, `owner_console` was imported lazily (first WhatsApp message, Telegram approval, or the daily keyword batch), so a fresh process had often not loaded it at all.
- **Fix:**
  - `backend/runtime_identity.py` (stdlib only), installed from `sitecustomize.py`, wraps `SourceFileLoader.get_code` for the watched modules (default `agents.owner_console`). It hashes the exact bytes it compiles and writes an atomic record to `/app/state/runtime_identity/<module>.<pid>.<starttime>.json`. The record ties pid, `/proc` start time and boot_id together, so a record from an earlier process cannot pass.
  - `routes/webhooks.py` now imports `agents.owner_console` at module import. An AST check confirmed the import has no side effects (definitions and env reads only).
  - `maintenance/runtime_identity_check.py --pid 1 --expect MOD=SHA` is read-only and exits 0 only on LOADED_MATCH.
  - Tests: `tests/test_runtime_identity.py` (8).
- **Restart:**
  - Preflight SAFE at 19:02.
  - `bash backend/scripts/pre_restart.sh` exit 0 at 19:02:57.
  - `docker restart autospare_backend` exit 0, 19:02:59→19:03:10.
  - Same container `5f1afa2e667f` and image `bf7efaf6`, RestartCount 0, no OOM.

  released** (`evidence/2026-10-28-release/e2e/result_cand3_before_fix.txt`, check C11). (Downstream `supplier_payments` has

  `UPDATE … SET consumed_at … WHERE id = … AND consumed_at IS NULL AND revoked_at IS NULL RETURNING id`, returns who won
  (InMemoryAuthStore equivalent); `payment_refusal` releases only when it wins, else refuses + audit event.
  Files: `supplier_authorization.py` `a58d44de…`, `procurement.py` `79d2d848…`, `tests/test_supplier_safety_gates.py`

## 2026-10-29 07:48 Israel — ONE customer price policy on every channel (owner top priority) — DEPLOYED, VERIFIED LIVE

Owner (2026-10-29): read the price policy and implement it in all price files and gates so every agent and customer
channel uses the same policy and shows the same price. Policy: `docs/PRICE_POLICY.md`; code: `backend/price_policy.py`.
Bundle `candidates/price-policy-2026-10-29/` (`SHA256SUMS` `e7ee401c…`, 15 files, +555/−298, `EVIDENCE.sha256` `41371d6e…`).

### What was wrong (each found in the code, then proven by a test that FAILED on the old code: 11 of 30)
1. **Different offers on different channels.** Website search priced a part from the cheapest *visible* offer
   (class-compatible first); the **chat** picked by supplier **priority, not price**, incl. unavailable offers; the
   **brands pages** the same; **wishlist/watch** from a different set (no listing filter, ILS-only); **NOA** from yet
   another set → the same part could show different prices per channel.
2. **The pre-charge check** (Stripe single + multi order) compared a VAT-INCLUSIVE live unit with the ex-VAT stored
   unit (every local-supplier order flagged "price changed" → 409 and its unit rewritten), re-priced from the cheapest
   offer of ANY supplier instead of the chosen one, and set shipping to the MAX fee (multi-supplier orders under-charged).
3. **Raw cost shown as a price.** Search payload carried `base_price` / `min_price_ils` / `max_price_ils` (catalog
   costs) and `cheapest/most_expensive_price_ils` = MIN/MAX of raw supplier cost; the website list fell back to
   `min_price_ils` (our cost) / `base_price` when no offer was priced.
4. **base_price as a customer price** with a flat 18%: compare-page fallback (also claimed "in stock, 3 days"),
   cart fallback, chat fallback (`total = base_price + a default fee`, and `base_price / 1.18` as if it held VAT).
5. **Two VAT rules for an unknown supplier** (agents 0%, search 18%) and a flat-18% default (`local_vat_only=False`).
6. **Rounding:** one-step `round(cost×1.45×(1+vat))` vs net and VAT rounded separately; WhatsApp checkout VAT on
   the rounded subtotal vs per-unit VAT × qty on its Stripe line; `int(x*100)` truncation for Stripe amounts.
7. **The website computed prices itself** (`cost×1.45`, flat `×0.18`) when the backend price was missing; labels said
   "VAT 18%" on 0%-VAT (foreign) prices; the search list showed the pre-VAT net while the detail/cart showed net+VAT.
8. Own `1.45`/`1.18`/`0.18` numbers in `orders.py`, `payments.py` (3×), agents (2×), NOA, issuing service, admin.

### Fix
`backend/price_policy.py` = the one rule (margin, conditional VAT incl. unknown → local, rounding, lines, delivery
once per supplier, agorot rounding, `VISIBLE_OFFER_SQL` / `ORDERABLE_OFFER_SQL` / `price_basis_order_sql`, no-offer
ESTIMATE from the importer cost — never `base_price`). Every surface calls it: `routes/parts.py` (search fields +
customer price range + compare list sorted by what the customer pays + estimate), `routes/cart.py`, wishlist/watch
(`_current_part_offer`), `routes/orders.py`, `routes/payments.py` (`_live_reprice_order` for both checkouts, WhatsApp
checkout, `_agorot`), `BACKEND_AI_AGENTS.py` (chat price functions, chat offer query, chat estimate),
`routes/brands.py`, NOA (`_noa_real_catalog_fact`, exact price), `services/stripe_issuing_service.py`, admin constants;
website `Parts.jsx` / `Orders.jsx` (no client formula, no raw fallback, VAT-inclusive list price, real VAT label).
Behaviour change to know: an order whose chosen offer is no longer orderable (unavailable / inactive supplier) gets
"unavailable" at payment instead of being silently re-priced from another supplier.

### #119 — PARTIAL (code fixed + verified; deploy, data repair and scheduler release await approval)
Root causes (traced in code, measured read-only on production 2026-10-31):
- `fix_base_prices` (cheapest available offer × 1.45, raise-only, ignored offer visibility) and `normalize_base_price`
  (importer × 1.45 for every part, also parts with offers; estimate order importer → online → max, unlike the policy) wrote
  different values to the same rows: 722,972 of 1,221,671 parts with a visible offer hold importer × 1.45 ≠ the offer net. On
  the isolated DB one part flipped ₪145 ↔ ₪116 on every run. Customer prices were never affected (no surface reads base_price).
- Cleanup-agent writers: the normalizer copied any (also foreign) offer cost into `importer_price_ils`/`max_price_ils`
  (69 live rows carry its signature); two recovery tasks wrote the raw USD cost (highest offer, no margin) / the scraped price.
- `merge_catalog_fitment_from_part_vehicle_fitment` ran per manufacturer and replaced a part's whole copy each time: a part
  fitting two makes kept the last one (563 of 563 already-copied multi-make parts list one make) and was rewritten every run.
- BMW/Ford/Jaguar backfills: unbounded fetchall; `except: pass` around inserts (one failure aborts the transaction silently);
  inserts counted on conflict; Jaguar re-read the same first 2,000 parts forever (1 of 164 matches reachable); Ford wrote
  "Ford Focus" — vehicle search accepts "focus" but never "ford focus" (12,360 rows / 12,156 parts invisible); `\bCONNECT`
  matched CONNECTION; Jaguar matched merchandise and classic-era cars (27 of its 32 live rows are wrong); BMW read tyre sizes
  as motorcycle codes R17/R18/R19 (644 live rows) and mapped U25 to "X2 Electric" (U25 = MINI Countryman, BMW X2 = U10; 95 rows).
Fix: one ownership rule `apply_base_price_rule` (policy net of the cheapest visible offer of the part's own class → owner
fix_base_prices; else the catalog estimate → owner normalize_base_price; other-class-only / no input → unchanged), used by both
tasks and the four cleanup writers; per-part fitment sync; shared bounded name-backfill runner; keyset batches + saved cursor,
SKIP LOCKED, time budget, counters scanned/eligible/updated/unchanged/skipped/failed/reasons. `price_policy.py` unchanged;
`docs/PRICE_POLICY.md` documents the rule. The six stay in `OOM_BLOCKED_TASKS` until A3.
Evidence (`evidence/`):
- Isolated DEBUG run, old vs new code, representative dataset (local/foreign/unknown/USD suppliers, competing, stale, URL-less,
  other-class, no-offer, multi-make, stale/dict/duplicate JSON, incomplete fitment, merchandise): new code — customer surfaces
  identical before/after, rerun and reverse order 0 rows changed, interrupted run resumes to the identical result, counters =
  rows changed; searches Ford Focus/Ranger, BMW 3 Series, MINI Clubman, Jaguar XF find their parts (old: Ford none, Lexus part
  loses Lexus, ping-pong on every rerun); prepared Ford repair makes the old prefixed row searchable.
- Tests: `test_maintenance_policy_alignment.py` (new) + `test_base_price_classification.py` (fixtures made explicit; G/I assert
  the ownership rule): 69 passed on the candidate; on the old code the behavioural ones fail (999 kept, 43.5 from a hidden offer,
  72.5 estimate order, 270 raw cost, ping-pong). Full regression by test identity vs deployed baseline: unit 2,865 common, 0
  outcome changes; isolated DB 563 common, 1 change (heavy fitment-merge contract test failure → pass); existing failures unchanged.
- Production dry run (read-only, the new code's own functions): base_price 1.35 M of ≈ 4.1 M scanned in 40 min — fix_base_prices
  would change 304,015 of 409,764 offer parts in the sample (≈ 0.91–0.93 M overall), normalize 27,538 of 232,851 (≈ 0.08–0.10 M);
  merge full pass 721,033 parts (5,983 multi-make restored); BMW 71 / Ford 298 / Jaguar 61 new rows (Jaguar reviewed by hand).
Remaining (approvals): A1 deploy; A2 `REPAIR_FITMENT.sql` (R1 12,360 Ford renames, R2 95 U25, R3 644 tyre rows, R4 27 Jaguar);
A3 `scheduler_A3.patch` (release + schedule, batch plan and stop conditions in DEPLOY.md).

Root cause (not "baseline also fails"): the process-global async SQLAlchemy engines (`engine`, `pii_engine`) keep pooled asyncpg connections bound to the event loop of the first test that used them; a later test (pytest-asyncio gives each its own loop) checks out such a connection -> "attached to a different loop". Reproduced independently: baseline and candidate, alone / module / exact pair in both orders / original full-suite order, 3x each (`evidence/regression_pair/PRE_FIX.*`). Fix: `tests/conftest.py` autouse fixture `_isolate_global_async_pools` drops the pooled connections before and after every test (`sync_engine.dispose(close=False)`) - no skip, no reorder, no retry, no relaxed assertion. Closure: alone 3/3, modules, pair both orders 3/3 (`POST_FIX_FINAL.candidate.matrix.txt`), full suite: neither test fails.

Sandbox DB row counts identical before/after the E2E modules (`evidence/importer_e2e/sandbox_counts_*`).

Mechanism (verified, not invented): `Agent` tool with `model:"opus"`, not `fork` (a fork ignores the model override); the prompt is the whole handoff because the agent starts cold; the result returns as a task notification; Claude reviews/re-tests/closes. **Handoff is not automatic** - Claude must make the call; the tool cannot physically prevent a third attempt, it makes the limit auditable: `candidates/.../process/debug_escalation.py` (ledger: `attempt` refuses vague/repeat attempts and exits 3 = ESCALATE after the 2nd failed attempt and = LOCKED for a 3rd; `handoff` refuses before 2 failures and writes the context package with the fixed safety constraints; 6 tests pass). Splitting one problem into several issue ids is not detectable by the tool. Doc: `process/DEBUG_ESCALATION.md`. Drill (`evidence/escalation_drill/`): scratch problem, two real failed attempts (7/8, 10/12), third attempt refused (rc=3), handoff built, Opus agent given only that package returned PASS 19/19 with its own root cause (a lone separator must follow a valid 1-3 digit leading group); Claude re-ran it (19/19, original 12 expectations unchanged) before accepting. Limitation: the drill proves the round trip on a toy problem, not a production bug.

## 2026-11-03 (night) — NOA reel: SkyReels motion + real-photo reel stored with the post (CODE-ONLY, NOT ACTIVATED; status PARTIAL)

**Goal (owner):** connect the new video model to NOA and verify NOA uses it. **Models/infra:** `Skywork/SkyReels-V2-I2V-1.3B-540P-Diffusers` on the owner's private ZeroGPU Space `autospare/autospare_video_test` (Wan2.2 POC removed; README `python_version: "3.12.12"` — ZeroGPU ignores 3.11; Dev Mode switched off to allow edits).
**Measured (2026-11-03):** one clip = ~300 s, 97 frames (~4 s), 544x960, 26 GB VRAM. Flat parts survive (brake pads); a spark plug became another object and an oil filter a gold mesh, a logo bleached and garbled text. Hence motion is allowed ONLY for `SKYREELS_SAFE_PARTS` (brake pad/disc/rotor); every other part and every failure = slow zoom of the REAL photo.
**Findings in the existing path (confirmed by reading the code):** (1) `registry.dispatch("tiktok")` downloaded ANY `media_url` and published it as video bytes, but NOA's `media_url` is the thumbnail+QR JPEG (never a video) — fixed (`_looks_like_video`); (2) NOA never kept the clean part photo (only the QR composite), (3) the template TikTok video used no part photo at all.
**Changes:** `social/video_gen.py` (`build_post_reel`, `make_noa_reel`, `skyreels_clip`, daily cap `SKYREELS_DAILY_MAX`=3 via Redis, fails closed; reel = 4.8 s motion/zoom + 5.6 s photo + 5.4 s QR end card, 15.0 s, 1080x1920, silent audio track); `BACKEND_API_ROUTES.py` (reel built at DRAFT time when `NOA_REEL_ENABLED=1` and tiktok is configured, stored as `thumbs/video/<sha>.mp4`, `video_key/video_url/video_ai` in post meta, preview line in the owner's WhatsApp approval message); `social/registry.py` (`dispatch(..., video_key=)` publishes the stored reel; key must start with `thumbs/video/`); `routes/admin.py` + `agents/owner_console.py` (pass `video_key`); `routes/thumbnails.py` (serves `thumbs/video/*.mp4` as video/mp4 so the owner can preview); `docker-compose.yml` (`SKYREELS_ENABLED`, `SKYREELS_DAILY_MAX`, `NOA_REEL_ENABLED`, all default OFF).
**Bug found while verifying (mine):** the Space reports the result `url` with an extra `/gr/` root that redirects to its home page; the first version accepted those 22,916 HTML bytes as a video, ffmpeg failed and the reel was dropped. Fixed: build the file URL from the path, require the `ftyp` MP4 signature, and fall back to the all-photo reel if a motion clip is unusable.
**Tests:** `tests/test_noa_reel.py` 12 passed (allowlist, off-by-default, 15 s vertical + audio, motion failure still yields a reel, unsafe part never calls the Space, stored reel is what TikTok receives, key outside the prefix ignored, image media_url never sent as video, the `/gr/` URL + non-MP4 regression, unusable clip fallback).
**Verification (isolated process in the backend container, TikTok publish and S3 upload STUBBED, nothing posted, nothing written to the bucket):** real catalog brake-pad photo + real SkyReels output from the Space -> `build_post_reel` (ai=True) -> `registry.dispatch("tiktok", video_key=...)` -> the stub received exactly the stored reel (1.27 MB, 15.0 s, 1080x1920, video+audio; Hebrew caption, car name, QR end card).

### #117 — web chat `send_message` has no owner check — FIXED IN CANDIDATE, VERIFIED IN ISOLATION, NOT DEPLOYED (PARTIAL)
- **Root cause (VERIFIED, reproduced):** `routes/chat.py::send_message` and the shared brain (`BACKEND_AI_AGENTS._process_user_message_impl`, and the background `_process_agent_response_for_message_impl`) loaded `Conversation.id == <client id>` with no `user_id` filter. Reproduced on real tables in the sandbox: attacker `process_user_message(attacker, …, victim_conv_id)` returned the victim's conversation id, wrote a message into it (message count 1 -> 2) and the victim's history reached the model.
- **Reach:** every path that resolves a conversation id: web `POST /api/v1/chat/message`, `POST /api/v1/chat/upload-audio` (passes the id into `process_user_message`), the background web agent, and (same function) the WhatsApp/Telegram durable path — those pass `user_key = str(conversation.user_id)` (`routes/webhooks.py:1611/1996`), so enforcing ownership there changes nothing legitimate. Also found: `POST /api/v1/chat/rate` attached a rating to any conversation id (integrity only, no read). NOT affected (checked): the websocket (echo only), `admin.py` conversation routes (admin-gated by design), and the other chat endpoints (already filter `Conversation.user_id`).
- **Fix:** ONE enforcement point `BACKEND_AI_AGENTS.load_owned_conversation(db, conversation_id, user_id)` — parses both ids as UUID, returns the conversation only if `user_id` owns it; missing/malformed/unknown/foreign all return None (no existence oracle). Used by the brain, the background variant, `send_message` (malformed id -> 422; foreign id behaves like unknown -> new conversation for the caller) and `rate_agent` (foreign -> 404).
- **Tests:** `tests/test_conversation_ownership.py` 20 cases (helper: own/foreign/missing/malformed/SQL-ish/unknown user; brain forged id; brain own-id still continues with history; background variant; `send_message` forged / own / none / malformed; `rate_agent` foreign 404 + own OK). Before fix: 17 failed / 3 passed; after: 20 passed. Isolated-only (sandbox DB); the PII-DB test users/conversations they create are left in the disposable DB like the other e2e tests.
- **Remaining exposure until deployed:** any authenticated, verified user who learns a victim's conversation UUID (random v4, not enumerable, but listed in admin views/logs) can write into and read-through that conversation. Production state: UNFIXED.

### #126 — Car-Parts.ie importer stores the Irish cost as an Israeli price input — FIXED IN CANDIDATE, VERIFIED IN ISOLATION, NOT DEPLOYED; DATA REPAIR NOT DONE (PARTIAL)
- **Root cause:** `importers/car_parts_ie_import_generic.py` INSERT bound the EUR->ILS cost (`price_eur × EUR_ILS_RATE`, converted once) to `importer_price_ils` AND `max_price_ils` (and `online_price_ils`, `min_price_ils`). `price_policy.catalog_estimate` reads `importer_price_ils` (then `max_price_ils/1.18`) as a LOCAL cost (+18% VAT); only `online_price_ils` is the foreign input (0%).
- **Measured on production (read-only, 2026-11-03):** the tracker's "273,966" is NOT reproduced. Car-Parts.ie has 754,529 offers/parts (754,470 active): `importer_price_ils>0` 753,111, `max_price_ils>0` 752,957, `online_price_ils>0` 752,528; only 323 have importer == max (see #127 — a second writer rewrote `max`). **Customer-visible impact is small:** a part with a visible Car-Parts.ie offer is priced from that offer at 0% VAT (correct). Parts with NO visible offer and no Israeli offer that therefore get the estimate on the foreign cost + 18% VAT: **1,300** active parts (tracker said 3,472; the number has moved). Opel importer (`opel_car_parts_ie_import.py`) writes NULL prices — not affected. Other car-parts.ie writers: none found.
- **Fix:** the importer now inserts `importer_price_ils = NULL` and `max_price_ils = NULL`, keeps `online_price_ils` / `min_price_ils` = the foreign cost and `base_price` = cost × 1.45 (the policy net, 0% VAT); the ON CONFLICT clause (with its audited `CASE WHEN EXCLUDED > 0` guard) therefore never overwrites an existing local cost with this source. `maintenance/audit_importers.py` output identical before/after (10 pre-existing errors, none new).
- **Tests:** `tests/test_pricing_integrity_126_128.py::test_importer_never_writes_a_foreign_cost_into_local_price_inputs` runs the REAL `import_file` on the sandbox (DSN overridden after an isolated-host assertion): 25 EUR × 4.0 -> online 100.00 once, importer/max NULL, base 145.00, estimate VAT 0; a re-import at a new price leaves a pre-existing local importer 77 / max 91 untouched. Baseline: fails (importer = 100.00). Plus `test_estimate_of_a_foreign_cost…` pins the 18% overcharge (171.10 vs 145.00).
- **Data repair — proposed, NOT run, needs owner approval:** for Car-Parts.ie-only parts set `importer_price_ils` / `max_price_ils` to NULL where they equal/derive from the Car-Parts.ie offer cost and no Israeli offer exists, so the estimate falls to `online_price_ils`; bounded batches, `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, per-row provenance. The 1,300 customer-affecting parts are the priority subset. Re-import alone does not repair existing rows.

### #127 — `refresh_min_max_prices` overwrites `max_price_ils` from any offer — FIXED IN CANDIDATE, VERIFIED IN ISOLATION, NOT DEPLOYED; POLICY CONFIRMATION REQUESTED (PARTIAL)
- **Root cause:** `db_update_agent.refresh_min_max_prices` (live in the 3×/day `run_all_tasks`) aggregated EVERY available offer — any supplier (active or not, internal/test included), any product class, price 0 — and wrote `min = MIN×1.18`, `max = MAX×1.18`, VAT applied to foreign offers too. Baseline reproduction: min 0.0 (a no-price offer) and max 10,620 (an unavailable other-class offer × 1.18).
- **Production sample (read-only):** in a 30,000-offer Car-Parts.ie sample 45% of the parts have `max = cost×1.18` (this task's signature), ~49% `max = cost` (the importer's); in a 300k-offer sample 208 of 278 mixed local+foreign parts have `max` = the highest offer of ANY supplier × 1.18.
- **Doc/code conflict (stated, not silently resolved):** `BACKEND_DATABASE_MODELS` column comment ("most expensive supplier incl. VAT") and `docs/skills.md` ("recalculates from supplier_parts") describe the legacy meaning; `price_policy.py`, `docs/PRICE_POLICY.md` and the deployed `db_cleanup_agent` (#119 A1, 2026-11-01) define `max_price_ils` as the IL consumer reference incl. 18% VAT, read by the estimate as a LOCAL cost, written only from a LOCAL offer. The fix follows the deployed, owner-approved policy; **owner please confirm** (then the two stale descriptions get corrected).
- **Fix:** only ORDERABLE offers (`price_policy.ORDERABLE_OFFER_SQL`: available, active supplier, not internal/test), positive cost (`price_ils`, else `price_usd × rate`), class-compatible (the cleanup agent's rank rule). `min_price_ils` = cheapest eligible offer with ITS OWN VAT (18% local, 0% foreign). `max_price_ils` = highest eligible LOCAL offer × 1.18, and left UNCHANGED when there is none. The local/foreign SQL is now ONE definition, `price_policy.local_supplier_sql()` (the cleanup agent's private copy now delegates to it). My first version had a real bug the test caught: `:vat` in `CASE … ELSE 1` was typed integer by Postgres (1.18 -> 1) — now `CAST(:vat AS numeric)`.
- **Tests:** mixed suppliers/classes/active/internal/unavailable/zero-price -> (50.0, 236.0) and unchanged on a repeated refresh; foreign-only never overwrites an existing max (400.0 / 118.0); a USD-only offer converted once. Baseline: 2 failures with the values above.
- **Still open inside #127 (not changed, decision needed):** the cleanup agent fills `max` from the LOWEST local offer when empty, this task from the HIGHEST local offer; `min_price_ils` has three writers (this task, the cleanup agent = raw any-supplier min, `services/ebay_price_sync`); `catalog_scraper.py:~2386` writes `min/max_price_ils` with a second formula (listed separately below). Existing wrong `max_price_ils` values stay until a data repair (not done, needs approval).

### #128 — unknown supplier country treated as foreign — DECISION REQUIRED; NO CODE CHANGE (OPEN)
- **Verified behaviour:** `price_policy.vat_rate`: no name AND no country -> local (matches the docs); a name with a NULL country -> local only if the name is in `LOCAL_SUPPLIER_NAMES` (`autoparts pro il`), else foreign; a non-empty country is local only if in `{il, israel, ישראל}` — so the literal placeholder `'Unknown'` is FOREIGN (0% VAT). `PRICE_POLICY.md` and the module docstring say "unknown supplier → local" and are only unambiguous for "no name and no country".
- **Measured on production (suppliers with offers only):** `Motorstore IL` (country `'Unknown'`, 4,396 offers, Israeli by name/history) is charged 0% VAT; `RockAuto` (country NULL, 3 offers, US) 0% VAT (correct). Active suppliers with country `'Unknown'` and 0 offers: Gates, Mann Filter, Meyle, Bilstein, Brembo (no impact today). All other offer-bearing suppliers have an explicit country.
- **Why no code change:** treating `'Unknown'`/NULL-with-a-name as local would fix Motorstore but put 18% on RockAuto and on every future foreign supplier whose country was never filled in — the opposite error. **Decision for the owner:** (A, recommended) fix the DATA — set `Motorstore IL.country='IL'`, `RockAuto.country='US'` (2 rows, approval needed) and add a health alert for an active supplier with offers and an empty/'Unknown' country; keep the rule that a known country decides. (B) change the code so unknown country with a name counts as local (VAT never dropped) and set RockAuto's country explicitly first. Behaviour is pinned by `test_unknown_country_placeholder_is_currently_foreign_decision_pending` so a later change is deliberate.

### #117 — conversation ownership (IDOR) — SECURITY TESTS PASS · FULL SUITE NO REGRESSION · ARTIFACT READY · **OPEN IN PRODUCTION**
- **Root cause (re-verified):** a client-supplied conversation id was loaded by id only (`send_message`, the audio upload, `process_user_message`, its background variant) and `rate_agent` attached ratings to any id.
- **Fix — files:** `BACKEND_AI_AGENTS.py` (`load_owned_conversation`, the ONE enforcement point; `process_user_message(..., trusted_conversation=False)`), `routes/chat.py` (`send_message`: malformed id → 422, foreign id behaves like unknown; `rate_agent`: foreign → 404), `routes/webhooks.py` (`_run_agent_for` is the only caller allowed `trusted_conversation=True`), tests `test_conversation_ownership.py` (26), stubs in `tests/chat_lifecycle_harness.py` + `tests/test_whatsapp_late_reply_e2e.py`.
- **Flaw found in my own first fix (audit 2026-11-03):** WhatsApp picks the conversation BY PHONE, not by user (`routes/webhooks.py:1246-1260`). A customer who chatted anonymously (conversation owned by the shared anonymous user) and then registered is served as the new user inside the old conversation; a pure owner check would have silently started a NEW conversation on every message and split the history. Reproduced by test (`_run_agent_for`, wa + tg), fixed with the server-only `trusted_conversation` flag; a guard test fails if any file other than `routes/webhooks.py` passes it. The first full run then failed ~40 WhatsApp lifecycle tests with `TypeError` (their `fake_agent` stubs lacked the new parameter) — stubs fixed and a signature-parity test added.
- **Paths audited (grep of every conversation/message read in the backend):** web chat, audio, background agent, shared brain, WhatsApp, Telegram, `/chat/rate` — all go through the one loader; the other `/chat/*` routes already filter `user_id`; admin routes are admin-gated by design; websocket is echo-only; history/memory loaders are only called with an ownership-checked `conversation.id`. No TOCTOU (ownership is immutable). No existence oracle (foreign == nonexistent; malformed → 422 only). Not changed: soft-deleted conversations are still loadable by their owner (pre-existing behaviour).
- **Tests:** 26 new pass (before the fix 17 of the first 20 failed); WhatsApp lifecycle + late-reply + ownership 71 passed. **Full suite, live + #117 only:** `python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q -rf tests --ignore=tests/test_full_system.py --ignore=tests/test_system.py` → **2643 passed, 74 skipped, 2 failed, exit 1**; the 2 failures reproduce identically on the unmodified tree and are environmental: `test_fitment_search_flows::test_search_by_license_plate_without_part_type_returns_grouped_shape` (needs a live server) and `test_harvester_health::test_P_compose_default_documentation_and_code_agree` (needs `docker-compose.yml` at `/`). Live-API files against a uvicorn started from the patched tree: **248 passed, 29 skipped, exit 0**. Not labelled PASS: 2 known environmental failures remain.
- **Artifact:** `01_PATCH_117_conversation_ownership.diff` sha256 `e96c2715eee5685914ee153583819d250629c03b134b9c87befc5c965ace05db`; dry-run clean on the current live tree; no migration/config/dependency; rollback `patch -p1 -R` + the same restart. ### #127 — `max_price_ils` / `min_price_ils` — CODE FIXED+VERIFIED IN ISOLATION · POLICY **UNAPPROVED** · DOCS PREPARED (not applied) · PRODUCTION UNCHANGED
- **Contract evidence (re-traced):** ~35 Israeli importers write `max_price_ils` as the published Israeli consumer price incl. 18% VAT (`import_kia_israel`, `colmobil_import_v2`, `samelet_import_v2`, …); `catalog_scraper` writes an Israeli Google-Shopping reference; the deployed cleanup agent fills it only from LOCAL offers. EVERY customer-facing read goes through `price_policy.catalog_estimate*` (`routes/parts.py`, `routes/cart.py`, the chat brain, `db_update_agent`) which reads it as a LOCAL cost (`max/1.18`); no payload exposes either column. `min_price_ils` has NO reader. The legacy "most/least expensive supplier incl. VAT" wording survives only in the `BACKEND_DATABASE_MODELS` comment, the DB column COMMENTs (`docs/schema/*.sql`; changing the DB comment is a production DDL write — not proposed) and `docs/skills.md`.
- **Recommended definition (needs owner approval):** `max_price_ils` = the **Israeli consumer reference in ILS incl. 18% VAT**, written only from local sources/eligible local offers, never from a foreign cost. **Amendment to the proposed wording:** VAT is NOT "per supplier country" for `max` — it is an Israeli reference by definition (always 18%); a foreign cost at 0% VAT in it would be divided by 1.18 again by the estimate. `min_price_ils` (internal, no reader) = cheapest eligible offer incl. the VAT that offer carries — the only column where per-country VAT applies.
- **Real examples (production read-only, 2026-11-03 20:52Z):** (a) Kia Israel OEM 267403C200: offer ₪47.00, stored max ₪55.46 = 47×1.18 ✔. (b) Car-Parts.ie BMW part: offer ₪71.53 (foreign), stored max=min ₪84.41 = ×1.18 ✘ — an estimate from that max would show ₪122.39 vs the correct foreign ₪103.72 (+18%). (c) sample of 6,000 recently-updated parts: all 5,789 foreign-only parts have max = foreign cost×1.18 (the old refresh's write; the fix would not write it — **existing values need a data repair**); of 211 mixed parts all equal the old rule and 11 would change under the fixed rule. (d) mixed OEM 16273: stored max ₪153.13 (= foreign ₪129.77×1.18) vs local cost ₪47.20 → fixed rule ₪55.70.
- **Fix — files:** `db_update_agent.refresh_min_max_prices` (eligible = `ORDERABLE_OFFER_SQL` + cost>0 + class-compatible; VAT per supplier via the single SQL form; `max` only from eligible LOCAL offers, else unchanged), `price_policy.local_supplier_sql` (shared with `db_cleanup_agent`, which now delegates), `BACKEND_DATABASE_MODELS` comments; docs diff for `docs/PRICE_POLICY.md` (new "Catalog cost columns" section marked PROPOSED) + `docs/skills.md`. VAT). Option B (blanket "unknown → local") rejected: it would put 18% on RockAuto and on every future foreign supplier whose country was never filled.
- **Built (guard, not the root fix):** `price_policy.country_problem()/country_problem_sql()` (2-letter code or Israel-by-name = usable; missing/placeholder/other = problem; Python and SQL forms proven equal on 27 cases), read-only task `db_update_agent.validate_supplier_countries` (registered in `TASK_REGISTRY` and the 3×/day list; flags ACTIVE suppliers with PRICED offers and a problem country, reports the VAT currently billed, one `notify_owner` per day via the existing alert path, never writes). ## 2026-11-05 — Owner post edits (WhatsApp + Telegram) never reached the post — **APPLIED ON DISK, NOT LIVE (backend not restarted)**
- **Root cause (VERIFIED):** no `social_posts` row had `content_version > 1`. (1) The WhatsApp console had no edit command, so free text went to the chat LLM, which cannot change a post. (2) The Telegram "✏️ ערוך" callback promised "send the corrected text — I'll save it" but stored nothing and nothing consumed the next message (it fell into the engagement inbox). `campaign_manager.update_post_content` was reachable only via the HTTP route in `routes/campaigns.py`.
- **Fix:** one authoritative `owner_console.edit_post_text()` → `update_post_content` (version bump, back to `pending_approval`, so an old approval can never publish edited text). WhatsApp: `ערוך <id> <text>`. Telegram: the button arms a one-hour `pending_edit` (AgentMemory `noa`), the owner's next plain message in the owner chat consumes it (`routes/webhooks.py`), and the button replies honestly if no post is pending. Help text updated.

- **Unresolved, unchanged (counted):** 25,251 parts (19,695 with conflicting signals, 5,503 no independent evidence, 53 in groups < 100) and 9,482 Mazda-text fitment rows still on Jaguar's id (their 342 parent parts have conflicting signals; models are Mazda models but the parent was not proven).
